entry.definition_en: felt, done, or shared equally by two or more people or sides, so that each gives and receives the same relation
entry.core_image: 两面相对的镜子：每一面都映出对方，也都被对方映出——交换的目光
entry.scene: After the split, the two founders signed a mutual agreement that neither would approach their old clients for a year.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 mutual 是「相互协议」（第 4 个义项：双方按同样条件达成的安排）；句意：分开之后，两位创始人签署了一份相互协议，约定一年内谁都不去接触原来的客户。图中可辨识物件：协议文件、两支笔、两把相对的椅子、公司标志、日历。

pos.zh: 相互的；彼此的
共同的；双方共有的
（mutuals）互助基金；互助公司

forms.label: 复数名词（互助基金／公司）

senses.title: A feeling shared both ways
senses.definition: felt by each of two people toward the other, so that each gives and receives the same feeling
senses.definitionCN: 两个人各自对对方怀有同样的感受，彼此给予也彼此接受
senses.example: Their mutual affection grew over the years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相互爱慕多年来日益加深。
senses.why: Latin mutuus means 'exchanged, reciprocal', from mutare 'to change, exchange'. A feeling is mutual when it travels both ways: each person hands it over and receives it back, like two mirrors facing each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mutuus 意为“交换的、相互的”，来自 mutare“改变、交换”。感情是 mutual，是因为它双向流动：每个人都交出去，又接回来，像两面相对的镜子。

senses.title: A shared person or thing: mutual friend
senses.definition: shared by two or more people, each of whom knows or has the same person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 由两个或更多人共同拥有，每人都认识或拥有同一个人或物
senses.example: We met through a mutual friend.
senses.exampleCN: 我们是通过一个共同的朋友认识的。
senses.why: Here the exchange is not of feeling but of possession: one friend sits in the middle and belongs to both. Reciprocity turns into a shared point, and the two separate links become one common link.
senses.whyCN: 这里交换的不是感情，而是“拥有”：一个朋友坐在中间，同时属于双方。相互性变成一个共享的节点，两条分开的关系连成一条共同的关系。

senses.title: Mutual fund: pooled investment
senses.definition: a pooled investment fund in which many investors own shares and share the returns
senses.definitionCN: 由许多投资者持有份额并共享收益的汇集投资基金
senses.example: She put her savings into a low-cost mutual fund.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄投入了一只低成本的共同基金。
senses.why: Money is exchanged into a common pool, and each investor's claim is reciprocal with the others. The name comes from the mutual ownership of the fund, not from a two-person swap.
senses.whyCN: 钱被交换进一个共同的池子，每个投资者的权利与其他人的权利相互对应。这个名字来自基金的共同所有权，而不是两个人的互换。

senses.title: Mutual agreement between two sides
senses.definition: an arrangement agreed by both sides, each accepting the same terms
senses.definitionCN: 双方共同商定、各自接受同样条款的安排
senses.example: They signed a mutual agreement not to compete.
senses.exampleCN: 他们签署了一份互不竞争的相互协议。
senses.why: An agreement is mutual when the same terms travel in both directions: each side gives a promise and receives one. Mutare 'exchange' becomes a legal exchange of obligations, with neither side above the other.
senses.whyCN: 协议是 mutual，是因为同样的条款双向流动：每一方都给出承诺，也收到承诺。mutare“交换”变成法律上的义务交换，没有一方凌驾于另一方。

senses.title: Mutual benefit: gain on both sides
senses.definition: benefiting both sides, so that each side's gain is tied to the other's
senses.definitionCN: 对双方都有利，每一方的收益都与另一方相连
senses.example: The partnership was based on mutual benefit.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合作关系建立在互利之上。
senses.why: Benefit is mutual when the gain travels both ways. The word marks symmetry of outcome rather than charity: each side's good is tied to the other's, so the exchange is fair in both directions.
senses.whyCN: 利益是 mutual，是因为好处双向流动。这个词标记的是结果的对称，而不是慈善：每一方的好处都与另一方相连，所以交换在两个方向上都公平。

senses.title: Mutual respect: given and received
senses.definition: respect that each party gives to the other and receives back
senses.definitionCN: 各方给予对方、同时也从对方得到的尊重
senses.example: A healthy team runs on mutual respect.
senses.exampleCN: 健康的团队依靠相互尊重运转。
senses.why: Respect here is the exchanged currency. It is not one person admiring another but a relation in which both look up and both are looked up to; the symmetry is what makes it 'mutual' rather than one-way.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尊重是交换的货币。它不是一个人仰慕另一个人，而是一种双方都仰视、也都被仰视的关系；正是这种对称使它成为“相互的”，而不是单向的。

senses.title: Mutual company: owned by members
senses.titleCN: 互助公司：由成员共同拥有
senses.definition: a company or insurer owned by its members, who share its profits or risks
senses.definitionCN: 由成员共同拥有、成员共享利润或风险的保险公司或企业
senses.example: A mutual insurer returned part of the premium to its members.
senses.exampleCN: 一家互助保险公司把部分保费返还给成员。
senses.why: The mutual company is owned by the people it serves: their roles as customer and owner are exchanged, so the same group sits on both sides of the counter. Mutuality becomes an ownership structure.
senses.whyCN: 互助公司由它所服务的人拥有：顾客与所有者的角色被交换，于是同一群人在柜台两边都坐着。mutual 的相互性由此变成一种所有权结构。

senses.title: Mutual misunderstanding: a shared failure
senses.definition: a misunderstanding in which each side misreads the other
senses.definitionCN: 双方各自误读对方的误解
senses.example: Mutual misunderstanding kept the talks frozen for months.
senses.exampleCN: 相互误解让谈判冻结了数月。
senses.why: Misreading also travels both ways. The reciprocity of mutuus does not make the result good; it only guarantees symmetry, so mutual can describe a shared failure as easily as a shared benefit.
senses.whyCN: 误读也会双向流动。mutuus 的相互性并不保证结果是好的，它只保证对称，所以 mutual 可以同样轻易地描述共同的失败，而不只是共同的好处。

senses.title: Two-way and equal in structure
senses.definition: two-way and reciprocal in structure, with each side occupying the same relation to the other
senses.definitionCN: 结构上双向、对等，每一方对另一方处于同样的关系
senses.example: The treaty created mutual obligations on both borders.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约在两个边境上都产生了相互义务。
senses.why: This is the bare structural sense: two arrows, equal and opposite. Mutare 'to change' is visible as exchange, and the suffix -uus turns the act of exchanging into a state of being exchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这是最赤裸的结构义：两支等长而方向相反的箭头。mutare“改变”在这里显现为交换，而后缀 -uus 把“交换的动作”变成“处于被交换的状态”。

intro.en: Mutual is a Latin adjective of exchange: mutare 'to change, exchange' → mutuus 'exchanged, reciprocal' → French mutuel → English mutual. English then adds -ly, -ity, -ism, -ist and -istic, and the sense spreads from two-way feeling to shared friends, pooled funds and member-owned companies.
intro.cn: mutual 是一个表示“交换”的拉丁形容词：mutare“改变、交换”→ mutuus“交换的、相互的”→ 法语 mutuel → 英语 mutual。英语随后加 -ly、-ity、-ism、-ist、-istic，词义从双向感情扩展到共同的朋友、共同基金和成员共有的公司。

items.en: Latin mutare is generally traced to PIE *mei- 'to change, exchange'. The reconstruction is accepted for the 'change' idea, though the exact prehistoric form and its other branches are less certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutare 一般追溯到原始印欧语 *mei-“改变、交换”。“变化”这一观念的重构被接受，但具体的史前形态及其在其他语支中的对应并不那么确定。

items.en: mutare means 'to change, exchange'. Its adjective mutuus means 'reciprocal, borrowed, exchanged', formed with the adjectival ending -uus. The derivation chain is therefore verb → adjective: the act of exchanging becomes the state of being exchanged.
items.cn: mutare 意为“改变、交换”。其形容词 mutuus 意为“相互的、借来的、交换的”，由形容词词尾 -uus 构成。因此派生链是动词 → 形容词：交换的动作变成“处于被交换的状态”。

items.en: English records mutual in the 1560s, borrowed from Middle French mutuel. The early sense is 'reciprocal, given and received', used of love, obligations and relations between persons or states.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 60 年代记录到 mutual，借自中古法语 mutuel。早期义为“相互的、给予并接受的”，用于爱、义务以及人与人、国与国之间的关系。

items.en: Mutual spreads into social and commercial language: mutual friend, mutual society, mutual improvement. Dickens's novel Our Mutual Friend (1864–65) made the phrase 'mutual friend' famous, though the phrase was already in use; this is a usage note, not the origin of the word.
items.cn: mutual 扩展到社会和商业语言：mutual friend、mutual society、mutual improvement。狄更斯的小说《我们共同的朋友》（1864–65）让 mutual friend 这个说法广为人知，但该短语此前已在使用；这是用法注记，不是词的起源。

items.en: Mutual fund and mutual company become standard financial terms, especially in the United States. The word now names a pooled or member-owned structure, so the 'exchange' idea is institutionalised rather than personal.
items.cn: mutual fund 和 mutual company 成为标准金融术语，尤其在美国。这个词现在命名一种汇集或成员共有的结构，于是“交换”的观念被制度化，而不再只属于个人。

items.en: Mutual + -ly gives mutually, + -ity gives mutuality, + -ism gives mutualism, + -ist gives mutualist, + -istic gives mutualistic. The semantic path is exchange → reciprocal → shared → two-way → pooled ownership, with no prefix at any stage; the word grows entirely by suffixation.
items.cn: mutual + -ly 产生 mutually，+ -ity 产生 mutuality，+ -ism 产生 mutualism，+ -ist 产生 mutualist，+ -istic 产生 mutualistic。语义路径是：交换 → 相互 → 共享 → 双向 → 汇集所有权；全程没有前缀，这个词完全靠加后缀生长。

note.en: The look-alikes share the mut- shape and mostly the mutare root, but mean different things; the near meanings differ in whether the emphasis is on exchange, sharing or structure.
note.cn: 形近词共享 mut- 外形且多与 mutare 同根，但意思不同；近义词的差别在于强调交换、共享，还是结构。

entries.definition: the adverb from mutual: in a way that is shared or reciprocal. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: mutual 派生的副词：以共享或相互的方式。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: able to change; changeable. It comes from the same mutare 'change' root but stresses change, not exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 能改变的；易变的。它来自同一个 mutare“改变”词根，但强调变化，而非交换。

entries.definition: an organism or gene that has changed. It shares mutare but points to biological change.
entries.definitionCN: 发生变异的生物体或基因。它与 mutare 同根，但指向生物学的变化。

entries.definition: given by each side to the other; corresponding in both directions. It is more formal and more exact than mutual.
entries.definitionCN: 双方互相给予的；两个方向相对应的。它比 mutual 更正式、更精确。

entries.definition: used or held by more than one person. It stresses common possession rather than two-way exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 由不止一人使用或拥有的。它强调共同拥有，而非双向交换。

entries.definition: belonging to or affecting several people at once. It is broader than mutual and does not require symmetry.
entries.definitionCN: 同时属于或影响几个人的。它比 mutual 更宽，不要求对称。

entries.definition: done or held by two or more people together. It stresses combined action rather than exchanged feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个或更多人共同做或共同拥有的。它强调联合行动，而非交换的感受。

entries.definition: operating in both directions. It is the plain structural word behind the final sense of mutual.
entries.definitionCN: 在两个方向上运作的。它是 mutual 最后一个义项背后最朴素的结构词。

normalIntro.en: These use the real mutare → mutuus chain and the actual social and financial collocations, without inventing a prefix that the word does not have.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 mutare → mutuus 派生链，以及真实的社会与金融搭配，不虚构这个词并不存在的前缀。

normal.en: mutare = to change or exchange; mutuus = exchanged, reciprocal. Exchanging is the core.
normal.cn: mutare = 改变或交换；mutuus = 交换的、相互的。交换就是核心。

normal.en: A mutual feeling travels both ways, like two mirrors facing each other.
normal.cn: mutual 的感情双向流动，像两面相对的镜子。

normal.en: A mutual friend is one shared point in the middle of two relationships.
normal.cn: mutual friend 是两段关系中间的一个共享节点。

normal.en: A mutual fund is a shared pool; a mutual company is owned by its members.
normal.cn: mutual fund 是一个共享的资金池；mutual company 由成员共同拥有。

normal.en: Mutuality and mutually keep the abstract noun and the adverb close to the same exchange idea.
normal.cn: mutuality 与 mutually 把抽象名词和副词都保持在与同一个“交换”观念附近。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows of equal length pointing at each other. Neither is longer; each gives what the other gives.
abstract.cn: 想象两支等长的箭头相向而指。没有一支更长；每一方给出的正是另一方给出的。

abstract.en: The same two arrows can mean love, respect, an agreement, a benefit or an obligation.
abstract.cn: 同样的两支箭头可以表示爱、尊重、协议、利益或义务。

abstract.en: Turn the arrows into a circle and many people can share one friend, one fund or one company, all owning and being owned at once.
abstract.cn: 把箭头围成一个圈，许多人就能共享一个朋友、一只基金或一家公司，同时拥有也被拥有。

examples.en: Their relationship works because the trust is mutual.
examples.cn: 他们的关系能维持，是因为信任是相互的。

examples.en: We were introduced by a mutual acquaintance at the conference.
examples.cn: 我们是在会议上由一位共同认识的人介绍的。

examples.en: The two countries reached a mutual understanding on fishing rights.
examples.cn: 两国就捕鱼权达成了相互谅解。

dict_mnemonic.text: “缪求偶”——求偶本来就是两个人相互的事 → mutual 相互的、双方的

entry.root: 拉丁 mutare“改变、交换”→ mutuus“交换的、相互的”→ 法语 mutuel → 英语 mutual；核心是“同一种关系在双方之间来回交换”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mutual all describe one relation running in two directions: a feeling, a friend, a fund, an agreement, a benefit, respect, a company, a misunderstanding and a bare structure of equal exchange.
sensesIntro.cn: mutual 的九个义项都描述同一种双向运行的关系：一种感情、一个朋友、一只基金、一份协议、一份利益、一份尊重、一家公司、一次误解，以及最赤裸的等量交换结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two equal arrows pointing at each other; whatever one side gives, the other side gives too.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支等长的箭头相向而指；一方给出什么，另一方也给出什么。

branches.en: FEELING: affection and respect travel both ways, so each person both gives and receives.
branches.cn: 感情：爱慕与尊重双向流动，每个人都既给予又接受。

branches.en: SHARED RELATION: one friend or one misunderstanding sits between two people, so the link is common rather than separate.
branches.cn: 共享关系：一个朋友或一次误解位于两人之间，所以这条联系是共同的，而不是各自分开的。

branches.en: POOLED OWNERSHIP: a fund or a company is owned by many members whose claims mirror one another.
branches.cn: 汇集所有权：基金或公司由许多成员共同拥有，彼此的权利相互映照。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: an agreement or obligation is mutual when the same terms apply in both directions.
branches.cn: 结构：当同样的条款在两个方向上适用时，协议或义务就是相互的。

branches.en: BENEFIT: gain is mutual when each side's advantage depends on the other's.
branches.cn: 利益：当每一方的好处都依赖另一方的好处时，利益就是互利的。

intro.en: Mutual has no prefix at all. It is a Latin adjective formed by a suffix (-uus) on a verb, and English builds every later word by adding another suffix: -ly, -ity, -ism, -ist, -istic, -ize and -ization.
intro.cn: mutual 完全没有前缀。它是拉丁动词加后缀 -uus 构成的形容词，英语后来的每一个词都靠再加后缀：-ly、-ity、-ism、-ist、-istic、-ize、-ization。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on mutare 'to change, exchange': mutuus 'exchanged, reciprocal', mutatio 'a change', mutabilis 'changeable'. The -uus ending turns the action into a state, which is why mutual feels like a condition rather than an event.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 mutare“改变、交换”上：mutuus“交换的、相互的”、mutatio“变化”、mutabilis“可变的”。-uus 词尾把动作变成状态，所以 mutual 感觉像一种状况，而不是一次事件。

items.meaning: in a reciprocal or shared way
items.meaningCN: 相互地；共同地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two plans are mutually exclusive.
items.exampleCN: 这两个方案相互排斥。

items.meaning: the quality of being reciprocal or shared
items.meaningCN: 相互性；共同关系（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The contract is built on mutuality of obligation.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同建立在义务的相互性上。

items.meaning: a system of mutual aid, or a biological relationship benefiting both species
items.meaningCN: 互助论；共生关系（-ism 表体系或主义）
items.example: Mutualism describes bees and flowers helping each other.
items.exampleCN: 共生关系描述蜜蜂与花朵互相帮助。

items.meaning: a supporter of mutual aid, or an organism in a mutually beneficial relationship
items.meaningCN: 互助论者；共生生物（-ist 表人或生物）
items.example: The fungus is a mutualist living on the roots.
items.exampleCN: 这种真菌是生活在根部的共生生物。

items.meaning: relating to a mutually beneficial relationship
items.meaningCN: 互助的；共生的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: Ants and acacia trees have a mutualistic bond.
items.exampleCN: 蚂蚁与金合欢树有一种共生关系。

items.meaning: to convert a company into member ownership
items.meaningCN: 使互助化；把公司转为成员共有（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The board voted to mutualize the insurer.
items.exampleCN: 董事会投票决定把这家保险公司改为互助制。

items.meaning: the process of converting to mutual ownership
items.meaningCN: 互助化过程（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: Mutualization gave policyholders a share of the company.
items.exampleCN: 互助化让保单持有人获得了公司的一份所有权。

items.meaning: not reciprocal; one-directional
items.meaningCN: 非相互的；单向的（non- 表否定）
items.example: A non-mutual agreement binds only one side.
items.exampleCN: 非相互的协议只约束一方。

entry.definition_en: to deny that something is true, to make something ineffective, or to cancel its force or value
entry.core_image: 一道删除线：在原本成立的句子上划一笔“不”
entry.scene: One faulty sensor negated months of careful calibration.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 negate 是「使失效、抵消」（第 2 个义项：使某事物的效力归零）；句意：一个故障传感器抵消了数月细致校准的成果。图中可辨识物件：传感器、校准曲线、被划掉的数据表。

pos.zh: 否认；否定；使无效；抵消

senses.title: Saying no to a claim
senses.definition: to deny that a statement or claim is true
senses.definitionCN: 否认某个陈述或主张是真实的
senses.example: The witness negated the claim that the car had stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 证人否认了那辆车曾停下的说法。
senses.why: Neg- is Latin 'not', and -ate makes a verb: to negate is literally to 'no' a statement. The denial is aimed at the truth of the words, not at any physical object.
senses.whyCN: neg- 是拉丁语“不”，-ate 使词成为动词：negate 字面就是“对一句话说不”。否认针对的是话语的真实性，而不是某个实物。

senses.title: Making something ineffective
senses.definition: to make a measure, device, or arrangement have no effect
senses.definitionCN: 使某项措施、装置或安排失去作用
senses.example: A power cut negated the security system.
senses.exampleCN: 一次停电让安保系统失效了。
senses.why: Saying no to an effect is the same gesture as saying no to a claim: the neg- particle moves from words to working force, so 'not true' becomes 'not working'.
senses.whyCN: 对一种效果说“不”，与对一句话说“不”是同一个动作：neg- 这个否定成分从“言语的真假”转到“作用的有无”，于是“不真”变成“不灵”。

senses.title: Grammar: marking a clause negative
senses.definition: to mark a clause or sentence as negative with a negative word or particle
senses.definitionCN: 用否定词或否定成分把分句或句子标为否定
senses.example: English negates the verb with 'not' or 'n't'.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用 not 或 n't 来否定动词。
senses.why: The Latin stem supplies the label: a clause carrying neg- is a clause that says no. The verb here names the grammatical operation, not a personal refusal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干提供的是标签：带有 neg- 的分句就是“说不”的分句。这里的动词指的是语法操作，而不是个人的拒绝。

senses.title: Voting a proposal down
senses.definition: to reject or cancel a proposal, motion, or official decision
senses.definitionCN: 否决或取消一项提案、动议或正式决定
senses.example: The board negated the proposal in a single vote.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会一次投票就否决了这项提案。
senses.why: A proposal is a sentence put forward for approval. Saying no to it in a formal vote is the institutional form of the same neg- denial.
senses.whyCN: 提案就是一句提交批准的话。在正式投票中对它说“不”，是同一个 neg- 否定在制度层面的形式。

senses.title: Cancelling out progress
senses.definition: to cancel the gain or advantage produced by earlier work
senses.definitionCN: 抵消先前努力带来的收益或优势
senses.example: The delay negated the lead they had built in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误抵消了他们在上半场建立的优势。
senses.why: Gains are treated as quantities that a later 'no' can remove. The root's negation becomes arithmetic: plus and minus cancel, so the verb means 'to wipe out the difference'.
senses.whyCN: 收益被当作可以被后来的“不”抹掉的量。词根的否定变成算术式的：正负相消，于是这个词表示“把差额抹平”。

senses.title: Logic: denying a proposition
senses.definition: to form the negation of a proposition, so that it has the opposite truth value
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个命题的否定，使其真值相反
senses.example: In logic, negating a proposition flips its truth value.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑中，否定一个命题会翻转它的真值。
senses.why: Logic takes the root's 'not' as an operator. Negation turns p into not-p; the verb names the act of applying that operator.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把词根的“不”当作运算符。否定把 p 变成非 p，这个动词指的就是施加该运算符。

senses.title: Overturning a hypothesis
senses.definition: to show that a hypothesis or assumption cannot stand
senses.definitionCN: 表明某个假设或前提无法成立
senses.example: The new data negated the hypothesis that the lake was lifeless.
senses.exampleCN: 新数据推翻了“湖中无生命”的假设。
senses.why: A hypothesis is a claim awaiting test. Evidence that says no to it negates it; the -ate verb again performs the refusal on a statement.
senses.whyCN: 假设是等待检验的主张。对它说“不”的证据就 negate 它；-ate 动词再一次对一句话执行拒绝。

senses.title: Self-negation: arguing against oneself
senses.definition: to contradict or cancel one's own earlier position or value
senses.definitionCN: 与自己的先前立场或价值相矛盾、相抵消
senses.example: The memoir negates its own boast by admitting the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这本回忆录取认了代价，从而否定了自己的夸耀。
senses.why: The neg- particle can turn inward: the same 'no' is aimed at the speaker's own statement. Reflexive negation is still denial, only the target has moved.
senses.whyCN: neg- 这个否定成分可以转向内部：同一个“不”对准说话者自己的话。反身否定仍然是否认，只是目标换了位置。

senses.title: Reducing value to zero
senses.definition: to bring a quantity, price, or value down to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 把数量、价格或价值降到零
senses.example: The write-off negated the asset's book value.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔核销使该资产的账面价值归零。
senses.why: The ultimate 'no' to a quantity is zero. At this end of the scale negation is not argument but arithmetic erasure, and the root's 'not' is read as 'none'.
senses.whyCN: 对一个量最终的“不”就是零。在这个尺度末端，否定不是辩论而是算术上的抹除，词根的“不”被读成“没有”。

intro.en: Negate is a Latin verb rebuilt in English from the stem of negare. The 1620s date is approximate; every later sense keeps the same negative particle and changes only what is being refused.
intro.cn: negate 是英语用 negare 的词干重新构成的拉丁式动词。17 世纪 20 年代的年代为大致估计；此后每个义项都保留同一个否定小品词，只改变“拒绝的对象”。

items.en: First recorded in English as a verb meaning 'to deny, contradict'. The related noun and adjective had entered earlier through French and Latin.
items.cn: 英语中最早于 17 世纪 20 年代记录为动词，义为“否认、反驳”；相关的名词和形容词此前已通过法语和拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: From Latin negare 'to deny, refuse, say no', a verb built on the negating particle neg- (also written nec-) plus the verb ending -are.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 negare“否认、拒绝、说不”，由否定小品词 neg-（也写作 nec-）加动词词尾 -are 构成。

items.en: The particle means 'not'. It appears as nec- before vowels and as neg- elsewhere; nec otium 'not leisure' became negotium 'business', the source of negotiate and negotiation. The same particle is the first element of renegade.
items.cn: 这个小品词意为“不”。在元音前作 nec-，其他位置作 neg-；nec otium“不闲”构成 negotium“事务、生意”，是 negotiate、negotiation 的来源。renegade 的第一个成分也来自同一否定。

items.en: Latin negatus is the past participle of negare. English takes Latin participial stems and adds -ate to make verbs (negate, navigate, locate), so negate = neg- + -ate, literally 'to perform the act of saying no'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 negatus 是 negare 的过去分词。英语取拉丁分词词干加 -ate 构成动词（negate、navigate、locate），故 negate = neg- + -ate，字面是“执行说不这一动作”。

items.en: The route runs from refusing a statement (17c) to making a legal instrument void (18c) to cancelling an effect or quantity (19c–20c). Each step keeps the same 'no' but changes what is refused: words, then validity, then force.
items.cn: 语义路径从拒绝一句话（17 世纪），到使法律文书作废（18 世纪），再到抵消效果或数量（19 至 20 世纪）。每一步都保留同一个“不”，只改变拒绝的对象：话语、效力，再到作用力。

items.en: Technical uses extend the same operator: logic negates propositions, grammar negates clauses, electronics and accounting negate signals and values. The noun negation and the agent noun negator name the act and the word that performs it.
items.cn: 技术用法延伸同一个运算符：逻辑否定命题，语法否定分句，电子与会计否定信号和数值。名词 negation 与施事名词 negator 分别命名这一动作和执行否定的词。

note.en: The first group checks spelling and root neighbours; the second separates near-synonyms by the kind of 'no' they express.
note.cn: 第一组检查拼写与词根近邻；第二组按“说不”的类型区分近义词。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to reach an agreement. It comes from negotium, literally 'not leisure' (nec otium), so it shares neg- but not the meaning of denial.
entries.definitionCN: 谈判以达成协议。它来自 negotium，字面“不闲”（nec otium），因此与 neg- 同源，但不含“否认”之义。

entries.definition: expressing denial, or less than zero. It is the adjective and noun built on the same neg- stem.
entries.definitionCN: 表示否定的，或小于零的。它是同一 neg- 词干构成的形容词和名词。

entries.definition: a person who abandons a cause. From re- 'again' + negare 'deny', literally 'one who denies again'.
entries.definitionCN: 背叛事业的人。来自 re-“再次”+ negare“否认”，字面“再次否认的人”。

entries.definition: to say that something is not true. It is the plain everyday verb; negate is more formal and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事不真实。它是最朴素的日常动词；negate 更正式，且常用于技术语境。

entries.definition: to make a legal act or agreement void. It stresses official cancellation.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律行为或协议无效。它强调官方层面的取消。

entries.definition: to remove the force or validity of something, often by showing a flaw.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物失去效力或有效性，常通过揭示缺陷来实现。

entries.definition: to stop a planned event or arrangement. It is broader and less formal than negate.
entries.definitionCN: 取消已计划的活动或安排。它比 negate 更宽泛、更口语。

entries.definition: to prove a claim false with evidence or argument; it stresses proof, not mere denial.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据或论证证明主张为假；它强调证明，而不只是否认。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations built on the real Latin particle and its real English relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想建立在真实的拉丁小品词及其真实英语同族词上，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: neg- is the Latin 'not'. Negate is the verb form: to put a 'no' on something.
normal.cn: neg- 是拉丁语的“不”。negate 是动词形式：给某物贴上“不”。

normal.en: negotium is nec otium, 'not leisure'. Business is 'not leisure', and negotiate shares the same neg- particle.
normal.cn: negotium 是 nec otium“不闲”。生意就是“不得闲”，negotiate 与它共用同一个 neg-。

normal.en: -ate is the ordinary Latin verb ending in English: negate, navigate and locate all name an action performed on a stem.
normal.cn: -ate 是英语里常见的拉丁动词词尾：negate、navigate、locate 都表示对词干执行某个动作。

normal.en: negative, negation and negator keep the same neg- stem; only the ending changes the job.
normal.cn: negative、negation、negator 都保留同一个 neg- 词干，只是词尾改变了它的语法工作。

normal.en: In logic and grammar the word is technical: a negator such as not, no or never negates a clause.
normal.cn: 在逻辑和语法里这个词是术语：not、no、never 这样的否定词（negator）否定一个分句。

abstract.en: Draw one clean line through a sentence on a page. The sentence is still there, but it no longer counts. That line is negate.
abstract.cn: 在纸上的一个句子中间画一道干净的线。句子还在，但它不再算数。这道线就是 negate。

abstract.en: Picture two waves meeting: the crest of one fills the trough of the other, and the surface goes flat. That is negation as cancellation.
abstract.cn: 想象两道波相遇：一道的波峰正好填进另一道的波谷，水面变平。这就是作为抵消的否定。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with equal weights on both sides: the pointer stops at zero, and the first weight can no longer move anything.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两边放着相等的砝码：指针停在零，最先放上的那个砝码再也推动不了任何东西。

examples.en: The new evidence appeared to negate the earlier findings.
examples.cn: 新证据似乎否定了早先的结论。

examples.en: Poor maintenance negated the benefits of the upgrade.
examples.cn: 维护不善抵消了升级带来的好处。

examples.en: A single 'not' can negate the whole clause.
examples.cn: 一个 not 就能否定整个分句。

dict_mnemonic.text: “你盖特”——你拿盖子一盖，把火苗和证据都盖灭 → negate 否认、使失效

entry.root: 拉丁 negare“说不、否认”，词干 neg-（nec-）=“不”；加 -ate 构成动词，核心是“对某事说不”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of negate are one act: the Latin particle neg- 'not' is applied to a statement, an effect, a proposal, a quantity, or the self.
sensesIntro.cn: negate 的九个义项其实是同一个动作：把拉丁否定成分 neg-“不”施加到一句话、一种效果、一项提案、一个数量或自我身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stroke of 'no' drawn across something that was standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一件原本成立的东西上划一道“不”。

branches.en: DENIAL: a statement or hypothesis is refused at the level of truth.
branches.cn: 否认：在真假层面拒绝一个陈述或假设。

branches.en: CANCELLATION: the same 'no' is aimed at an effect or at accumulated progress, so force is wiped out.
branches.cn: 抵消：同一个“不”指向某种效果或已积累的进展，作用力被抹掉。

branches.en: LOGIC AND GRAMMAR: the 'no' becomes an operator inside a clause or proposition.
branches.cn: 逻辑与语法：“不”变成一个分句或命题内部的运算符。

branches.en: VETO: a formal vote turns the denial into an institutional decision.
branches.cn: 否决：正式投票把否认变成制度性决定。

branches.en: INWARD AND ZERO: the 'no' can face the speaker or reduce a value to nothing.
branches.cn: 向内与归零：“不”可以朝向说话者自身，也可以把数值降到零。

intro.en: Negate is not built with a living English prefix. Its two parts are Latin: the negative particle neg- and the verb ending -ate. English borrowed the finished stem and afterwards adds ordinary derivational suffixes.
intro.cn: negate 不是由活的英语前缀构成的。它的两个成分都是拉丁语：否定小品词 neg- 和动词词尾 -ate。英语借入的是成品词干，之后才加普通派生后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin negare belongs to a small negation family: neg- / nec- 'not', negatio 'a denial', negativus 'that denies', and negotium 'business' from nec otium 'not leisure'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 negare 属于一个小的否定词族：neg- / nec-“不”、negatio“否认”、negativus“表示否定的”，以及由 nec otium“不闲”构成的 negotium“事务、生意”。

items.meaning: the act of denying, or the negative counterpart of a proposition
items.meaningCN: 否认的行为；命题的否定形式（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The word 'not' forms the negation of the sentence.
items.exampleCN: not 这个词构成该句子的否定形式。

items.meaning: expressing denial; less than zero; a negative image
items.meaningCN: 表示否定的；负的；负像（-ative 构成形容词和名词）
items.example: The test came back negative.
items.exampleCN: 检测结果呈阴性。

items.meaning: a word or person that negates
items.meaningCN: 否定词；否定者（-or 表示施事）
items.example: In English, 'not' is the most common negator.
items.exampleCN: 在英语中，not 是最常见的否定词。

items.meaning: able to be denied or cancelled
items.meaningCN: 可否定的；可被抵消的（-able 表示能够被……）
items.example: The claim is negatable by a single experiment.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张用一次实验就能被否定。

items.meaning: expressing a denial or refusal
items.meaningCN: 表示否定或拒绝的（-atory 构成形容词，较罕用）
items.example: The board issued a negatory reply.
items.exampleCN: 董事会作出了一份否定的答复。

items.meaning: one who denies or abandons a former cause
items.meaningCN: 再次否认、背弃原事业的人；叛徒
items.example: He was branded a renegade after leaving the party.
items.exampleCN: 退党之后，他被人称为叛徒。

items.meaning: to do business and discuss terms
items.meaningCN: 谈生意；谈判（经由 negotium“不闲”而来）
items.example: The two sides negotiated a ceasefire.
items.exampleCN: 双方谈判达成停火。

items.meaning: the process of discussing terms
items.meaningCN: 谈判过程（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The negotiation lasted three days.
items.exampleCN: 谈判持续了三天。

items.meaning: denied, cancelled, or made ineffective
items.meaningCN: 被否认的；被抵消的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The effect was negated by the delay.
items.exampleCN: 这一效果被延误抵消了。

entry.definition_zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉；联网
entry.definition_en: a system of connected people, machines, or places, or to connect such things and build personal contacts
entry.core_image: 一张渔网：许多绳结被细线穿连成一张可承力的面
entry.scene: The city's tram network links the old port to the new university district.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 network 是「交通网络」（第 5 个义项：线路互联的运输系统）；句意：这座城市的电车网络把老港区与新的大学城区连接起来。图中可辨识物件：电车轨道、站点连线、港口吊机、大学建筑。

pos.zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉；广播网
联网；建立人脉

derivatives.zh: 网；网状物（复合词的第一部分）

senses.title: A connected system
senses.definition: a group of things or people that are connected and operate as one system
senses.definitionCN: 由相互连接的事物或人组成、作为一个系统运作的整体
senses.example: The utility network delivers power to five counties.
senses.exampleCN: 这个公用事业网络向五个县供电。
senses.why: Network is net + work, 'a work made like a net'. The first sense is the literal one: separate units become one structure because strands run between them.
senses.whyCN: network 是 net + work，“像网一样编成的构造”。第一个义项就是字面义：独立单元因为之间有连线而成为同一个结构。

senses.title: A computer network
senses.definition: a set of computers linked so that they can share data and resources
senses.definitionCN: 为共享数据和资源而连接起来的一组计算机
senses.example: The lab's network went down during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间实验室的网络断了。
senses.why: Cables and wireless links take the place of the net's strands, and machines take the place of knots. The compound's structure transfers unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 线缆和无线链路取代了网绳，机器取代了绳结，但这个复合词的结构原封不动地转移过来。

senses.title: An online social network
senses.definition: an online platform on which users are linked to one another
senses.definitionCN: 用户之间彼此连接的网络平台
senses.example: Teenagers spend hours on social networks every day.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年每天花几个小时在社交网络上。
senses.why: People become the knots, and friend or follow links become the strands. The platform supplies the mesh; the users supply the connections.
senses.whyCN: 人成了绳结，好友或关注关系成了网绳。平台提供网面，用户提供连接。

senses.title: A broadcast network
senses.definition: a group of radio or television stations that broadcast under one organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一机构下播出节目的一组广播或电视台
senses.example: The network will air the final on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 该电视网将在周六播出决赛。
senses.why: One signal is distributed through many stations, exactly as one net is spread through many knots. The organization is the work, the stations are the mesh.
senses.whyCN: 一个信号通过许多台站分发出去，正如一张网铺开成许多绳结。机构是“构造”，台站是“网面”。

senses.title: A transport or road network
senses.definition: a system of routes, lines, and stops connected for transport
senses.definitionCN: 为运输而连接起来的线路、轨道与站点系统
senses.example: A dense rail network makes it easy to travel without a car.
senses.exampleCN: 密集的铁路网让人不必开车也能方便出行。
senses.why: Routes are the strands and stations are the knots. This is the 19c extension, when railways and telegraph lines were first described as networks.
senses.whyCN: 线路是网绳，站点是绳结。这是 19 世纪的延伸：铁路和电报线最早被称作 network。

senses.title: Personal and professional contacts
senses.definition: the set of people a person knows and can call on for help or information
senses.definitionCN: 一个人认识并能在需要时求助或获取信息的一群人
senses.example: His network helped him raise the funds in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他的人脉帮他在一周内筹到了资金。
senses.why: Here the mesh is social: each contact is a node, and introductions are the strands. 'Work' survives as the effort of maintaining the links.
senses.whyCN: 这里的网面是社会性的：每个联系人是一个结点，引荐就是连线。“work”则保留为维护这些连接所付出的工夫。

senses.title: To network: link or build contacts
senses.definition: to connect systems, or to build professional contacts deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 把系统连接起来，或有意识地建立职业人脉
senses.example: She networks with investors at every conference she attends.
senses.exampleCN: 她每参加一个会议都会与投资者建立联系。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into action: to network is to do the work of laying strands between nodes, whether cables or people.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转成的动作：network 就是做“在结点之间铺线”这件活，无论线是电缆还是人际关系。

senses.title: A neural network
senses.definition: a computing model of connected units loosely inspired by brain cells
senses.definitionCN: 一种由相互连接的单元构成、粗略模仿脑细胞的计算模型
senses.example: The network learned to recognize faces after thousands of examples.
senses.exampleCN: 在看过数千个样本后，这个网络学会了识别人脸。
senses.why: Artificial units are the knots and weighted connections are the strands. The name is a deliberate metaphor from the same mesh image.
senses.whyCN: 人工单元是绳结，带权重的连接是网绳。这个名称是有意从同一张网面意象借来的隐喻。

senses.title: The network effect
senses.definition: the way a service becomes more valuable as more people or devices join it
senses.definitionCN: 随着更多人或设备加入，某项服务的价值反而上升的现象
senses.example: The app's dominance comes from network effects, not from its design.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的主导地位来自网络效应，而不是它的设计。
senses.why: In a mesh, every new knot creates more possible strands. The compound network effect names that arithmetic: value grows with the number of connections.
senses.whyCN: 在一张网里，每个新绳结都会带来更多可能的连线。复合词 network effect 命名的正是这种算术：价值随连接数量增长。

intro.en: Network is a native English compound, not a Latin derivative. Its earliest sense was a net-like fabric; the modern system senses grew by metaphor from 19c transport and 20c media and computing.
intro.cn: network 是英语本族复合词，不是拉丁派生词。它最早指像网一样的织物；现代“系统”诸义则是从 19 世纪交通、20 世纪媒体与计算领域逐步隐喻扩展而来。

items.en: First recorded as a noun for a net-like fabric or mesh, especially a knotted net used for fishing, hair, or ornament. The word described a made object before it described an abstract system.
items.cn: 最早记录为名词，指像网一样的织物或网眼结构，尤指捕鱼、束发或装饰用的结网。这个词先指一件做出来的实物，后来才指抽象系统。

items.en: Net goes back to Old English net(t), from Proto-Germanic *natja- 'net'. It is a native Germanic word with no Latin source.
items.cn: net 可追溯至古英语 net(t)，来自原始日耳曼语 *natja-“网”。它是本族日耳曼词，没有拉丁来源。

items.en: Work goes back to Old English weorc 'deed, action, thing made', from Proto-Germanic *werka-. In compounds it means 'structure, construction', as in framework and network.
items.cn: work 可追溯至古英语 weorc“行为、行动、做成的物件”，来自原始日耳曼语 *werka-。在复合词中它表示“结构、构造”，如 framework 与 network。

items.en: The two free words were joined as network, modelled on 'a work made like a net'. No prefix or suffix is involved, and the word is not formed from a Latin stem. This is why its plural and verb forms are the plain English ones.
items.cn: 这两个自由词直接组合成 network，构词理据是“像网一样编成的构造”。其中没有前缀或后缀，也不是由拉丁词干构成，因此它的复数和动词形式都是普通英语形式。

items.en: From the 1840s–60s the word was applied to interconnected railways, canals, and telegraph lines. A network became any system of linked routes or stations, and the metaphor moved from fabric to infrastructure.
items.cn: 19 世纪 40 至 60 年代，这个词被用于互联的铁路、运河和电报线。network 由此指任何由线路或站点连接而成的系统，隐喻从织物转向基础设施。

items.en: Radio and television networks date from the 1920s; computer networks from the 1960s (ARPANET, 1969). The verb to network 'link systems, cultivate contacts' is a 20c development, and networking as a business activity became common in the 1970s–80s. Network effect is a later economics term.
items.cn: 广播网和电视网始于 20 世纪 20 年代；计算机网络始于 20 世纪 60 年代（ARPANET，1969）。动词 network“连接系统、经营人脉”是 20 世纪的产物，作为商业活动的 networking 在 70 至 80 年代流行起来。network effect 则是更晚的经济学术语。

note.en: The first group separates the base word and its close formations; the second compares other words for linked structures.
note.cn: 第一组区分基础词与紧密派生形式；第二组比较其他表示“连接结构”的词。

entries.definition: a mesh of cords with open spaces; the first element of network.
entries.definitionCN: 带网眼的绳线网；network 的第一个成分。

entries.definition: the activity of linking systems or building professional contacts; the -ing noun from network.
entries.definitionCN: 连接系统或建立职业人脉的活动；network 加 -ing 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the global computer network, usually capitalized; network is the generic word inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 全球计算机网络，通常大写；network 是包含在其中的通称。

entries.definition: a net of fine threads, especially a spider's web; also the World Wide Web. It stresses fine threads rather than an organized system.
entries.definitionCN: 细丝织成的网，尤指蛛网；也指万维网。它强调细丝，而不强调有组织的系统。

entries.definition: a network of wires or threads with open spaces; it is more concrete and usually smaller than a network.
entries.definitionCN: 带网眼的金属丝或线网；它比 network 更具体，通常也更小。

entries.definition: a regular pattern of lines, or a power or transport grid. It stresses even spacing.
entries.definitionCN: 规则的线条格局，或电力网、交通网。它强调均匀的间距。

entries.definition: a set of parts working together. It is the most abstract and does not require visible links.
entries.definitionCN: 共同运作的一组部分。它最抽象，也不要求有可见的连接线。

entries.definition: a central connection or link between things; formal and usually singular.
entries.definitionCN: 事物之间的中心联结；正式用语，通常用单数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real English words and the real historical extensions of the compound.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实的英语单词，以及这个复合词真实的历史扩展。

normal.en: net + work: a work made like a net — knots plus strands.
normal.cn: net + work：像网一样编成的活计——绳结加网绳。

normal.en: A fishing net is the oldest picture: holes and threads, but together they hold a catch.
normal.cn: 渔网是最古老的画面：有洞也有线，合起来却能兜住一网鱼。

normal.en: 19c railways and telegraphs turned 'net' into a system of routes.
normal.cn: 19 世纪的铁路和电报把“网”变成了线路系统。

normal.en: A social network links people; to network is to do the work of making those links.
normal.cn: 社交网络连接人；动词 network 就是做“建立这些连接”的活。

normal.en: Network effect: each new node adds links, so the whole becomes more useful.
normal.cn: 网络效应：每个新结点都会增加连接，于是整体变得更有用。

abstract.en: A fisherman's net thrown over water: separate knots, one surface.
abstract.cn: 一张撒在水面上的渔网：各自独立的绳结，却构成同一个网面。

abstract.en: A spider's web: no single strand carries the web; the pattern does.
abstract.cn: 一张蛛网：没有哪一根丝独自撑起整张网，撑起它的是图案本身。

abstract.en: A subway map: coloured lines and interchange dots, a city drawn as a net.
abstract.cn: 一张地铁图：彩色线路与换乘圆点，把整座城市画成一张网。

examples.en: The hospital is part of a regional network of clinics.
examples.cn: 这家医院是地区诊所网络的一部分。

examples.en: She networks with investors at every conference she attends.
examples.cn: 她每参加一个会议都会与投资者建立联系。

examples.en: One failed router can cut a whole computer network.
examples.cn: 一个路由器故障就能切断整个计算机网络。

dict_mnemonic.text: net（网）+ work（编成的活计）＝ 一张编好的网，结点相连 → 网络；再引申为人脉与联网

entry.root: 英语本族复合词：net“网”+ work“构造、活计”，字面“像网一样编成的东西”，核心是“结点与连线”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of network all keep one picture: separate knots held together by strands, whether the strands are cables, routes, broadcasts, or relationships.
sensesIntro.cn: network 的九个义项都保留同一幅画面：各自独立的绳结被网绳连在一起，无论这些绳子是电缆、线路、广播信号还是人际关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many knots joined by strands, so that no point stands alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多绳结被网绳连接，没有一个点是孤立的。

branches.en: PHYSICAL MESH: utilities and transport are routes and stations linked into one system.
branches.cn: 物理网面：公用设施与交通是把线路和站点连成的同一个系统。

branches.en: MACHINES AND MODELS: computers and neural units are nodes joined by connections.
branches.cn: 机器与模型：计算机和神经单元都是被连接起来的结点。

branches.en: PEOPLE: online platforms and personal contacts are social knots tied by links.
branches.cn: 人：在线平台和个人联系人都是被关系连起来的社交绳结。

branches.en: MEDIA: a broadcast network distributes one signal through many stations.
branches.cn: 媒体：广播电视网把一个信号分发到许多台站。

branches.en: ACTION AND VALUE: the verb links the knots, and the effect makes every new link worth more.
branches.cn: 动作与价值：动词做的是把绳结连起来，网络效应则让每条新连接更值钱。

intro.en: Network has no prefix or suffix: it is a compound of two free English words. Later formations either add ordinary suffixes or combine the noun with another noun.
intro.cn: network 没有前缀或后缀：它是两个英语自由词构成的复合词。后来的形式要么加普通后缀，要么与另一个名词再组合。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for network. Latin does have words for a net and for a binding — rete 'net' (the source of reticulate) and nexus 'a tying together' — but neither produced this word.
latinIntro.cn: network 没有拉丁语来源。拉丁语确有表示“网”和“联结”的词——rete“网”（reticulate 的来源）和 nexus“绑在一起”——但这两个词都没有产生 network。

items.meaning: the activity of linking systems or building professional contacts
items.meaningCN: 联网；人脉拓展（-ing 构成活动名词）
items.example: Networking is part of the job.
items.exampleCN: 拓展人脉是这份工作的一部分。

items.meaning: connected into a network
items.meaningCN: 联网的；接入网络的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: All the offices are networked.
items.exampleCN: 所有办公室都已联网。

items.meaning: a person skilled at building professional contacts
items.meaningCN: 善于建立人脉的人（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: She is a skilled networker.
items.exampleCN: 她是一个很会经营人脉的人。

items.meaning: a mesh of cords used to catch or hold things
items.meaningCN: 网；网状物（古英语 net(t)，复合词的基础）
items.example: The net was full of fish.
items.exampleCN: 网里装满了鱼。

items.meaning: net-like material or fabric
items.meaningCN: 网眼织物；网材（-ing 构成材料名词）
items.example: The fence is covered with netting.
items.exampleCN: 围栏上覆着网眼布。

items.meaning: the worldwide system of linked computer networks
items.meaningCN: 互联网（inter-“之间”+ net，由 internetwork 缩略）
items.example: The internet connects millions of networks.
items.exampleCN: 互联网连接着数以百万计的网络。

items.meaning: a standard for wired local computer networks
items.meaningCN: 以太网（ether + net 的复合词，有线局域网标准）
items.example: The office runs on Ethernet.
items.exampleCN: 这间办公室使用以太网。

items.meaning: a smaller network inside a larger one
items.meaningCN: 子网（sub-“在下、之内”+ network）
items.example: Each department uses a subnetwork.
items.exampleCN: 每个部门使用一个子网。

items.meaning: the gain in value as more users join a network
items.meaningCN: 网络效应：用户越多，网络价值越高
items.example: The platform thrives on the network effect.
items.exampleCN: 这个平台靠网络效应壮大。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 网；网状物（与 network 同义，但并非其词源）
联结；连接（也不是 network 的来源）

entry.definition_zh: 中立的；中性的；空挡的；无明显特征的
entry.definition_en: not supporting either side, not strongly marked, neither acid nor alkaline, or disengaged from a mechanism
entry.core_image: 天平正中的指针：两边等重，针停在零刻度
entry.scene: The mediator stayed neutral while both sides described the dispute.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 neutral 是「不站边的」（第 1 个义项：不偏向任何一方）；句意：双方陈述争议时，调解人保持中立。图中可辨识物件：天平、停在中线的指针、两侧等重的砝码、会议桌。

pos.zh: 中立的；中性的；空挡的；无强烈特征的
中立者；（汽车的）空挡

derivatives.zh: 中立主义者；中立主义的

senses.title: Not taking sides in a dispute
senses.definition: not supporting one side or the other in an argument or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在争论或冲突中不支持任何一方
senses.example: The mediator stayed neutral while both sides described the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 双方陈述争议时，调解人保持中立。
senses.why: ne + uter means 'neither of the two'. A neutral person refuses to be counted as either one, so the word begins with a refusal of both sides.
senses.whyCN: ne + uter 意为“两者中的哪一个都不”。中立者拒绝被算作任何一方，因此这个词的起点是“两边都不选”。

senses.title: Fair and unprejudiced
senses.definition: showing no bias when judging a matter
senses.definitionCN: 判断事情时不表现出偏向
senses.example: A neutral observer should hear both accounts before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 公正的观察者应先听完双方说法再作判断。
senses.why: The same 'neither' is applied to bias rather than to sides. The judgement is not tilted toward either party, and that lack of tilt reads as fairness.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“两者皆非”从“不选边”转到“不偏袒”。判断不向任何一方倾斜，这种不倾斜就被读作公正。

senses.title: A neutral country
senses.definition: a state that does not ally with either side in a war
senses.definitionCN: 在战争中不与任何一方结盟的国家
senses.example: Switzerland remained neutral during both world wars.
senses.exampleCN: 瑞士在两次世界大战中都保持中立。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a political status. A nation places itself outside the pair of opposing alliances, so it is officially neither ally nor enemy.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成一种政治身份。国家把自己置于两个对立同盟之外，因此官方上既不是盟友也不是敌人。

senses.title: A neutral colour
senses.definition: a colour that is muted or between extremes, such as beige, grey, or white
senses.definitionCN: 柔和或处于极端之间的颜色，如米色、灰色或白色
senses.example: The room was painted in neutral tones of beige and grey.
senses.exampleCN: 房间刷成了米色和灰色这样的中性色调。
senses.why: In colour, 'neither' means neither strongly warm nor strongly cool. The hue steps back to the middle so that other colours can stand out.
senses.whyCN: 在颜色上，“两者皆非”意味着既不强烈偏暖也不强烈偏冷。色调退到中间，好让其他颜色显出来。

senses.title: Chemically neutral
senses.definition: neither acidic nor alkaline, with a pH of about 7
senses.definitionCN: 既非酸性也非碱性，pH 约为 7
senses.example: Pure water is neutral, with a pH of about 7.
senses.exampleCN: 纯水呈中性，pH 约为 7。
senses.why: The balance image becomes chemical: hydrogen and hydroxide ions are present in equal strength, so neither acid nor base dominates.
senses.whyCN: 天平的意象变成化学式的：氢离子与氢氧根离子强度相等，因此酸和碱都不占上风。

senses.title: Neutral gear
senses.definition: a gear position in which the engine is disconnected from the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 发动机与车轮断开连接的挡位
senses.example: He left the car in neutral and let it roll slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车挂到空挡，让它慢慢滑行。
senses.why: Mechanically, the gearbox is neither in a forward nor a reverse ratio. Power is connected to neither path, which is the literal 'neither of two' inside a machine.
senses.whyCN: 机械上，变速箱既不在前进挡也不在倒挡。动力不接到任何一条路径，这正是机器内部的字面“两者皆非”。

senses.title: A neutral tone or register
senses.definition: a way of speaking or writing that avoids strong emotion or marked style
senses.definitionCN: 避免强烈情绪或明显风格的口头或书面表达方式
senses.example: She reported the conflict in a neutral tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用中性的语气报道了这场冲突。
senses.why: The voice takes neither emotional extreme and stays at the midpoint. Nothing in the delivery pushes the listener toward one reading.
senses.whyCN: 声音不取任何情绪极端，停在中间点。表达方式中没有任何东西把听者推向某一种解读。

senses.title: A neutral particle
senses.definition: a subatomic particle with no electric charge
senses.definitionCN: 不带电荷的亚原子粒子
senses.example: The neutron is electrically neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 中子不带电。
senses.why: In physics the 'neither' is electrical: the particle carries neither positive nor negative charge, so an electric field does not push it.
senses.whyCN: 在物理中，“两者皆非”指的是电性：粒子既不带正电也不带负电，因此电场不会推动它。

senses.title: A declared neutral stance
senses.definition: a public position of not joining either side, especially in policy or debate
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在政策或辩论中公开表示不加入任何一方的立场
senses.example: The union adopted a neutral stance on the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 工会对这次合并采取了中立立场。
senses.why: This is the stance rather than the person: a position is placed between the two camps and then declared. The 'neither' is now a policy, not a mood.
senses.whyCN: 这里指立场而不是人：把一种位置放在两个阵营之间并公开宣布。此时的“两者皆非”是一项政策，而不是一种心态。

intro.en: Neutral comes from Latin neuter 'neither of two', a compound of ne 'not' and uter 'one or the other of two', plus the adjective suffix -alis. English used it first in grammar, then in politics, science, and machines.
intro.cn: neutral 来自拉丁语 neuter“两者皆非”，由 ne“不”与 uter“两者之一”复合，再加形容词后缀 -alis。英语先把它用于语法，再扩展到政治、科学与机械。

items.en: First recorded in English as an adjective meaning 'belonging to neither of two extremes; not taking sides'. Grammatical uses for the neuter gender came through the same Latin family.
items.cn: 15 世纪晚期最早记录为形容词，义为“不属于两个极端中的任何一个；不站边”。语法上表示“中性”的用法也经由同一个拉丁词族进入英语。

items.en: From Latin neutralis 'of the neuter gender, neutral', an adjective formed from neuter.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 neutralis“中性的、中立的”，是由 neuter 构成的形容词。

items.en: neuter = ne 'not' + uter 'either of two, one or the other'. Literally 'neither the one nor the other'. The negative ne is the same particle seen in null and in ne- words such as nefarious.
items.cn: neuter = ne“不”+ uter“两者之一、或此或彼”，字面“既非此也非彼”。否定成分 ne 也见于 null 以及 nefarious 等含 ne- 的词。

items.en: Latin -alis forms adjectives from nouns, and English keeps it as -al. The path is neuter → neutralis → neutral, with the final Latin ending dropped in English.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -alis 由名词构成形容词，英语保留为 -al。路径是 neuter → neutralis → neutral，进入英语时去掉了拉丁词尾。

items.en: The earliest English uses were grammatical, for the neuter gender. By the 16c–17c the word extended to persons, judges, and states that join neither side: the grammatical 'neither' became a social and political one.
items.cn: 英语最早用于语法，指中性。到 16 至 17 世纪，这个词扩展到不加入任何一方的人、法官和国家：语法上的“两者皆非”变成了社会与政治上的“两者皆非”。

items.en: Chemistry adopts neutral for pH 7 (17c–19c), physics for particles with no charge (19c–20c), and motoring for the gear between forward and reverse (20c). Each is the same 'neither' applied to a new pair of opposites.
items.cn: 化学用 neutral 指 pH 7（17 至 19 世纪），物理用它指不带电的粒子（19 至 20 世纪），汽车业用它指前进与倒挡之间的空挡（20 世纪）。每一次都是把同一个“两者皆非”套用到一组新的对立面。

note.en: The first group traces the root and its derivatives; the second distinguishes words that also mean 'not on a side'.
note.cn: 第一组追溯词根及其派生词；第二组区分同样表示“不站边”的词。

entries.definition: grammatically neither masculine nor feminine; also having no sexual organs. It is the Latin source noun of neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性；也指无性器官的。它是 neutral 的拉丁语源名词。

entries.definition: the state of not taking sides, or the condition of being chemically neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 不站边的状态，或化学中性的状态。

entries.definition: to make something neutral, especially to cancel its effect or balance an acid.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变为中性，尤指抵消其作用或中和酸。

entries.definition: not favouring any side; it stresses fairness in judging.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方；强调判断时的公正。

entries.definition: free from prejudice; it stresses the absence of a prior leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 没有偏见；强调事先没有倾向。

entries.definition: not interested or concerned; unlike neutral, it often implies a lack of caring.
entries.definitionCN: 不感兴趣或不关心；与 neutral 不同，它常暗示冷漠。

entries.definition: emotionally distant and objective; it stresses separation from the matter.
entries.definitionCN: 情感上疏离而客观；强调与事情本身拉开距离。

entries.definition: not allied with any major power; a political term for states.
entries.definitionCN: 不与任何大国结盟；用于国家的政治术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pair ne + uter and the real modern applications of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁组合 ne + uter，以及这个词真实的现代应用。

normal.en: ne + uter = 'neither of the two'. Neutral starts by refusing both options.
normal.cn: ne + uter =“两者皆非”。neutral 的起点是把两个选项都拒绝。

normal.en: In grammar, neuter is the gender that is neither masculine nor feminine; neutral is the same idea as an adjective.
normal.cn: 语法中 neuter 是既非阳性也非阴性的性别；neutral 就是同一想法作形容词。

normal.en: pH 7 is neutral: neither acid nor alkali wins.
normal.cn: pH 7 是中性：酸和碱都不占上风。

normal.en: Neutral gear connects the engine to neither forward nor reverse.
normal.cn: 空挡让发动机既不通向进挡，也不通向倒挡。

normal.en: Neutrality is the noun for a country's legal status of not joining a war.
normal.cn: neutrality 是名词，指一国不参战的法律地位。

abstract.en: A balance needle stops exactly at the centre because the two pans carry equal weight.
abstract.cn: 天平指针正好停在正中，因为两个托盘等重。

abstract.en: A grey swatch sits between warm red and cool blue, belonging fully to neither.
abstract.cn: 一块灰色色样位于暖红与冷蓝之间，不完全属于任何一边。

abstract.en: A gear lever rests in the middle slot, connected to nothing, and the car simply rolls.
abstract.cn: 挡杆停在中间槽位，不接通任何传动，汽车只是滑行。

examples.en: Switzerland remained neutral during both world wars.
examples.cn: 瑞士在两次世界大战中都保持中立。

examples.en: The room was painted in neutral tones of beige and grey.
examples.cn: 房间刷成了米色和灰色这样的中性色调。

examples.en: Pure water is neutral, with a pH of about 7.
examples.cn: 纯水呈中性，pH 约为 7。

dict_mnemonic.text: ne（不）+ uter（两者之一）→ 两个都不是 → 中立、中性、空挡

entry.root: 拉丁 ne“不”+ uter“两者之一”=“两者皆非”，加 -al 构成形容词；核心是“不属于任何一边、不偏任何极端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of neutral all apply one Latin formula, ne + uter 'neither of two', to sides, bias, nations, colours, acids, gears, voices, charges, and declared positions.
sensesIntro.cn: neutral 的九个义项都在套用同一个拉丁公式 ne + uter“两者皆非”，只是对象分别是阵营、偏见、国家、颜色、酸碱、挡位、语气、电荷与公开立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle stopping exactly between two equal weights.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针正好停在两个等重砝码之间。

branches.en: POLITICS AND JUDGEMENT: a person, a judge, or a declared policy refuses to be counted on either side.
branches.cn: 政治与判断：个人、法官或公开政策拒绝被算入任何一方。

branches.en: A STATE'S STATUS: a country places itself outside the pair of opposing alliances.
branches.cn: 国家身份：一国把自己置于两个对立同盟之外。

branches.en: APPEARANCE AND VOICE: colour and tone stay at the middle register so nothing is pushed to an extreme.
branches.cn: 外观与声音：颜色和语气停在中间区段，不被推向任何极端。

branches.en: SCIENCE: pH 7 balances acid and base, and a neutral particle carries no charge.
branches.cn: 科学：pH 7 让酸与碱平衡，中性粒子不带电荷。

branches.en: MACHINE: the gearbox sits between two ratios and is connected to neither.
branches.cn: 机械：变速箱停在两个传动比之间，两个都不接通。

intro.en: Neutral is a Latin adjective stem plus the suffix -al. The negative element ne- is Latin, not a living English prefix, so the word is best read as ne + uter + -al rather than as an English prefixation.
intro.cn: neutral 是拉丁形容词词干加后缀 -al。否定成分 ne- 是拉丁语，不是活的英语前缀，因此最好把它读作 ne + uter + -al，而不是英语前缀构词。

latinIntro.en: The family turns on the pair ne 'not' and uter 'either of two'. Latin neuter and neutralis are the direct ancestors; the English derivatives add -ity, -ism, -ist, -ly, -ize and -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族围绕 ne“不”与 uter“两者之一”这一对成分展开。拉丁语 neuter 与 neutralis 是直系祖先；英语派生词则添加 -ity、-ism、-ist、-ly、-ize 与 -ation。

items.meaning: the state of not taking sides, or of being chemically neutral
items.meaningCN: 中立状态；中性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The treaty guaranteed the country's neutrality.
items.exampleCN: 该条约保障了这个国家的中立。

items.meaning: in a neutral manner
items.meaningCN: 中立地；不带倾向地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He described the meeting neutrally, without blaming anyone.
items.exampleCN: 他不带倾向地描述了会议，没有指责任何人。

items.meaning: a policy of staying out of conflicts between other powers
items.meaningCN: 中立主义（-ism 构成政策名词）
items.example: Neutralism shaped the country's foreign policy.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义塑造了该国的外交政策。

items.meaning: a supporter of neutralism
items.meaningCN: 中立主义者（-ist 表示人或形容词）
items.example: The neutralist bloc refused to join either alliance.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义阵营拒绝加入任何一个同盟。

items.meaning: to make neutral, cancel, or balance
items.meaningCN: 使中和；使无效；抵消（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: An alkali can neutralize an acid.
items.exampleCN: 碱可以中和酸。

items.meaning: the act or process of neutralizing
items.meaningCN: 中和；抵消的过程（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The neutralization of the acid took only seconds.
items.exampleCN: 酸的中和只花了几秒钟。

items.meaning: something that neutralizes
items.meaningCN: 中和剂；抵消物（-er 表示施事物）
items.example: The lab keeps a chemical neutralizer on hand.
items.exampleCN: 实验室常备一种化学中和剂。

items.meaning: neither masculine nor feminine; the source noun of neutral
items.meaningCN: 中性的；既非阳也非阴（neutral 的源名词）
items.example: Latin has a neuter gender for some nouns.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语中有些名词属于中性。

latinEntries.meaning: either of two, one or the other
neither of the two; of the neuter gender

entry.definition_en: in spite of that; however; used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or concedes what has just been said
entry.core_image: 一道路标：上面写着“到此为止”，箭头却继续指向前方
entry.scene: The forecast warned of storms; nevertheless, the expedition set out at dawn.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 nevertheless 是「尽管如此」（第 1 个义项：前文情况不阻止后文发生）；句意：预报警告有暴风雨，尽管如此，探险队仍在黎明出发。图中可辨识物件：暴风雨云、出发的队伍、指向前方的路标、被风吹动的旗。

pos.zh: 尽管如此；然而；不过（承接上文的让步或转折）

derivatives.zh: 尽管如此（与 nevertheless 近义）
然而；尽管如此（古旧或方言变体）
更少的；更少地（构词成分）

senses.title: In spite of what was just said
senses.definition: used to say that the next statement is true despite what has just been mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示尽管前文已提及某种情况，后文仍然成立
senses.example: The forecast warned of storms; nevertheless, the expedition set out at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 预报警告有暴风雨，尽管如此，探险队仍在黎明出发。
senses.why: The three old words say 'never the less': the fact just mentioned does not make the next fact any less true. The phrase denies a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 三个旧词说的是“never the less”：刚提到的事实并没有让后一个事实减少一分真实。这个短语否认的正是“减少”。

senses.title: Concede a point, keep the main claim
senses.definition: used to admit a fact and then assert the main point that survives it
senses.definitionCN: 用于先承认某个事实，再提出未被它推翻的主要观点
senses.example: The plan is expensive; nevertheless, it is the only workable one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划很贵，尽管如此，它是唯一可行的方案。
senses.why: Never (not ever) plus the less (to a smaller degree): the concession is admitted, but the main claim is not lowered by it. That is concession without surrender.
senses.whyCN: never（从不）加 the less（更少）：让步被承认，但主要主张并没有因此降低。这就是让步而不放弃。

senses.title: Contrast two facts
senses.definition: used to place two facts side by side when the first does not cancel the second
senses.definitionCN: 用于把两个事实并置，表示前者并没有取消后者
senses.example: The north of the island is cold; nevertheless, the south stays mild.
senses.exampleCN: 岛北部很冷，然而南部依然温和。
senses.why: Two facts are put on the same scale. The first does not lower the second, so the word marks contrast rather than defeat.
senses.whyCN: 两个事实被放在同一把尺子上。前者没有把后者压低，因此这个词标记的是对比，而不是击败。

senses.title: Formal written 'however'
senses.definition: a formal connective meaning 'however', common in reports and academic prose
senses.definitionCN: 意为“然而”的正式连接词，常见于报告和学术写作
senses.example: The results were inconclusive. Nevertheless, the committee recommended further study.
senses.exampleCN: 结果并不明确。然而，委员会建议继续研究。
senses.why: Register is the only difference here: the same 'not less' formula is used as a formal signpost between two sentences.
senses.whyCN: 这里唯一的差别是语域：同一个“并不更少”的公式被用作两个句子之间的正式路标。

senses.title: The earlier claim still holds
senses.definition: used when counterevidence exists but does not make an earlier claim false
senses.definitionCN: 用于虽有反证、但先前的说法并未因此失效的情况
senses.example: The evidence is thin. Nevertheless, the claim may still be true.
senses.exampleCN: 证据很单薄。尽管如此，这一说法仍可能是真的。
senses.why: The degree of truth is not diminished: 'not the less' means 'none the less'. The claim loses nothing from the weakness around it.
senses.whyCN: 真实的程度没有被削减：“not the less”就是“none the less”。这一说法并没有因为周围的薄弱而损失什么。

senses.title: Sentence-initial turn
senses.definition: a conjunctive adverb placed at the start of a sentence, usually followed by a comma
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首的连接副词，后面通常用逗号
senses.example: Nevertheless, no one voted against the motion.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管如此，没有人投票反对这项动议。
senses.why: Position is part of this sense: the adverb works as a hinge at the sentence boundary, turning the reader toward a contrasting point.
senses.whyCN: 位置本身就是这个义项的一部分：这个副词在句子边界处充当铰链，把读者转向一个形成对照的论点。

senses.title: Interchangeable with nonetheless
senses.definition: used as a synonym of nonetheless, especially in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 作为 nonetheless 的同义词使用，尤其在正式书面语中
senses.example: In most sentences, nevertheless can replace nonetheless without a change of meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 在大多数句子里，nevertheless 可以替换 nonetheless 而意思不变。
senses.why: Nonetheless is the same frame with non- (none) in place of never; both mean 'not the less'. The two are parallel formations, not unrelated words.
senses.whyCN: nonetheless 是用 non-（none）替换 never 的同一框架；两者都表示“not the less”。它们是平行构式，而不是互不相关的词。

senses.title: The old literal sense: 'not the less'
senses.definition: the historical literal meaning 'not any the less', before the phrase became a single adverb
senses.definitionCN: 在凝固为单个副词之前，短语的字面历史义“一点也不更少”
senses.example: In Middle English the phrase meant 'not the less' before it hardened into one word.
senses.exampleCN: 在中古英语中，这个短语在凝固成一个词之前意思是“not the less”。
senses.why: Read the parts literally: never = not ever, the = that, less = smaller. The phrase negates any reduction in degree.
senses.whyCN: 按字面读各个部分：never = 从不，the = 那个，less = 更少。整个短语否定的是程度上的任何减少。

senses.title: Emphatic concessive turn
senses.definition: a strongly marked concessive turn, often reinforced by still or even
senses.definitionCN: 语气较强的让步转折，常由 still 或 even 加强
senses.example: It was a difficult year; nevertheless, they still finished the project.
senses.exampleCN: 那是艰难的一年，尽管如此，他们还是完成了项目。
senses.why: Emphasis adds 'still' to the same denial of reduction. The speaker insists that the difficulty made the achievement no smaller.
senses.whyCN: 强调只是给同一个“否认减少”加上 still。说话者坚持：困难并没有让成就缩小一分。

intro.en: Nevertheless is an English phrase that became a word, not a Latin derivative. It is never + the + less, literally 'not the less'. Its nearest Latin-style parallel, nihilominus 'none the less', is a parallel formation rather than its source.
intro.cn: nevertheless 是一个凝固成词的英语短语，不是拉丁派生词。它由 never + the + less 构成，字面是“not the less”。拉丁语中最近的平行说法 nihilominus“none the less”只是平行构式，并非它的来源。

items.en: First recorded in writing as the phrase never the less, used adverbially to mean 'notwithstanding'. It competed with the shorter natheless and with the later nonetheless.
items.cn: 14 世纪晚期最早以短语 never the less 见于书面语，作副词表示“尽管如此”。它与更短的 natheless 以及后来出现的 nonetheless 并存竞争。

items.en: never goes back to Old English nǣfre, from ne 'not' + ǣfre 'ever' — literally 'not ever'. The ne- is the old Germanic negative also seen in neither and none.
items.cn: never 可追溯至古英语 nǣfre，由 ne“不”+ ǣfre“曾经”构成，字面“从不”。其中的 ne- 是古老的日耳曼否定成分，也见于 neither 和 none。

items.en: the is the definite article used inside an old comparative frame ('the less' = 'by that much less'). less comes from Old English lǣssa, the comparative of a word for 'small'.
items.cn: the 是定冠词，用在古老的比较框架中（“the less”=“按那个程度更少”）。less 来自古英语 lǣssa，是表示“小”的词的比较级。

items.en: The three words fused into a single adverb and were written as one word from the 16c–17c. Stress settled on the final syllable -less, and the literal sense 'not any the less' became the concessive sense.
items.cn: 这三个词在 16 至 17 世纪凝固为单个副词并连写成一个词。重音落在最后一个音节 -less 上，字面义“一点也不更少”由此转为让步义。

items.en: There is no Latin prefix or suffix in this word. Unlike negate or neutralize, it is a lexicalized native English phrase: never, the and less are all free English morphemes. Its Latin look-alike nihilominus is only a semantic parallel.
items.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁前缀或后缀。与 negate、neutralize 不同，它是一个词汇化的英语本族短语：never、the、less 都是英语自由语素。拉丁语中形似的 nihilominus 只是语义平行说法。

items.en: The same frame yields nonetheless (non- 'none' + the + less) and archaic natheless. Modern English restricts nevertheless mainly to formal and written registers, often at a sentence boundary with a following comma.
items.cn: 同一框架还产生 nonetheless（non-“none”+ the + less）和古旧的 natheless。现代英语主要把 nevertheless 限制在正式和书面语域，常置于句子边界并后接逗号。

note.en: The first group splits the phrase into its parts and its closest parallel; the second compares connectives with different shades of contrast.
note.cn: 第一组拆解短语的成分及其最接近的平行形式；第二组比较不同转折色彩的连接词。

entries.definition: a near-synonym meaning 'in spite of that'. It uses the same frame with non- (none) in place of never.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“尽管如此”的近义词，用同一框架，只是把 never 换成 non-（none）。

entries.definition: not ever; the first free element of nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 从不；nevertheless 的第一个自由成分。

entries.definition: smaller in amount or degree; the final free element of nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度更小；nevertheless 的最后一个自由成分。

entries.definition: used to introduce a contrasting statement. It is more neutral than nevertheless and can mark simple contrast as well as concession.
entries.definitionCN: 用于引出形成对照的陈述。它比 nevertheless 更中性，既可表让步，也可表单纯对比。

entries.definition: in spite of that. It is almost interchangeable with nevertheless, often slightly more formal and compact.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此。它几乎可与 nevertheless 互换，往往略更正式、更紧凑。

entries.definition: continuing up to now or despite something. It stresses persistence rather than a logical turn.
entries.definitionCN: 直到现在仍继续，或尽管有某事仍如此。它强调持续，而不是逻辑转折。

entries.definition: nevertheless; used as a short, often literary or emphatic connective.
entries.definitionCN: 然而；用作简短、常偏文学或强调的连接词。

entries.definition: in spite of this; very formal, and also used as a preposition before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此；非常正式，也可作介词置于名词前。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations split the word into its real historical parts and compare its real parallel formations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把这个词拆成真实的历史成分，并对照它真实的平行构式。

normal.en: Split it as never-the-less: 'not the less', meaning the previous fact does not make the next fact smaller.
normal.cn: 拆成 never-the-less：“not the less”，意思是前一个事实没有让后一个事实变小。

normal.en: None the less is the same idea; nonetheless uses non- where nevertheless uses never.
normal.cn: none the less 是同一个意思；nonetheless 在 nevertheless 用 never 的位置用了 non-。

normal.en: Never itself is ne + ever, 'not ever' — the same old negative as in neither and none.
normal.cn: never 本身是 ne + ever，“从不”——与 neither、none 中相同的古老否定。

normal.en: 'The less' is an old comparative frame, like 'so much the less'.
normal.cn: “the less”是古老的比较框架，类似“so much the less（因此更少那么多）”。

normal.en: In formal writing it usually stands at the start of a sentence with a comma: Nevertheless, ...
normal.cn: 在正式写作中它通常位于句首并后接逗号：Nevertheless, ...

abstract.en: A road sign reads 'no way through', yet the arrow on it keeps pointing forward.
abstract.cn: 一块路标写着“此路不通”，但上面的箭头仍指向前方。

abstract.en: Rain hits a flag, but the flag does not drop any lower. The weather adds weight without lowering the cloth.
abstract.cn: 雨打在一面旗上，旗子却没有降得更低。天气增加了重量，却没有把布压低。

abstract.en: A weight is added to one pan of a balance, and the other pan does not move down at all.
abstract.cn: 在天平一端加了一个砝码，另一端却一点也没有下沉。

examples.en: The path was steep; nevertheless, they reached the summit before noon.
examples.cn: 山路陡峭，尽管如此，他们还是在中午前到达了山顶。

examples.en: He was tired; nevertheless, he finished the report.
examples.cn: 他很累，尽管如此，他还是完成了报告。

examples.en: The evidence is thin. Nevertheless, the claim may still be true.
examples.cn: 证据很单薄。尽管如此，这一说法仍可能是真的。

dict_mnemonic.text: never（从不）+ the + less（更少）→ 一点也不更少 → 尽管如此

entry.root: 英语短语 never + the + less 的词汇化，字面“not the less（并不更少）”；核心是“前面的事没有让后面的事减少一分”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of nevertheless all rest on one literal formula, 'not the less': what came before may be admitted, but it does not reduce what comes after.
sensesIntro.cn: nevertheless 的九个义项都建立在同一个字面公式“not the less”上：前面的事可以承认，但它不会让后面的事减少一分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weight placed on one side that does not lower the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一端放上重物，另一端却不会因此下沉。

branches.en: CONCESSION: admit the obstacle, then insist that the main point is not lowered by it.
branches.cn: 让步：承认障碍，然后坚持主要观点没有因此被压低。

branches.en: CONTRAST: two facts sit on the same scale, and the first does not cancel the second.
branches.cn: 对比：两个事实放在同一把尺子上，前者没有取消后者。

branches.en: REGISTER AND POSITION: the same formula becomes a formal signpost at a sentence boundary.
branches.cn: 语域与位置：同一公式变成句子边界处的正式路标。

branches.en: PERSISTENCE OF TRUTH: counterevidence does not make the earlier claim any less true.
branches.cn: 真相的持续：反证并没有让先前的说法减少一分真实。

branches.en: PARALLEL FORM AND LITERAL ORIGIN: nonetheless repeats the frame, and the old parts still spell out 'not the less'.
branches.cn: 平行形式与字面来源：nonetheless 重复同一框架，而旧成分仍拼出“not the less”。

intro.en: Nevertheless is not built with prefixes or suffixes. It is a lexicalized three-word phrase, and its parts are free morphemes. Later English makes new words by substituting one component, as in nonetheless.
intro.cn: nevertheless 不是由前缀或后缀构成的。它是一个词汇化的三词短语，各成分都是自由语素。后来的英语通过替换其中一个成分来造新词，如 nonetheless。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this word. Latin expresses the same concessive idea with tamen 'nevertheless' and nihilominus 'none the less'; these are semantic parallels only, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源。拉丁语用 tamen“然而”和 nihilominus“none the less”表达同样的让步概念；它们只是语义平行说法，不是祖先。

items.structure: non- 'none' + the + less (same frame as nevertheless)
items.meaning: in spite of that
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此（与 nevertheless 同一框架，non- 替换 never）
items.example: The road was closed; nonetheless, we arrived on time.
items.exampleCN: 道路封闭了，尽管如此，我们还是准时到达。

items.meaning: nevertheless; archaic or dialectal
items.meaningCN: 然而；尽管如此（古旧或方言收缩形式）
items.example: Natheless, the old custom survived in the village.
items.exampleCN: 尽管如此，这一旧习俗仍在村子里留存。

items.meaning: not ever, at no time
items.meaningCN: 从不；在任何时候都不
items.example: He never spoke of the accident again.
items.exampleCN: 他再也没有谈起那场事故。

items.meaning: smaller in amount or degree
items.meaningCN: 数量或程度更小；更少
items.example: This version costs less than the other.
items.exampleCN: 这个版本比另一个便宜。

items.meaning: never again
items.meaningCN: 不再；永不再（文学复合词）
items.example: The raven said, 'Nevermore.'
items.exampleCN: 那只渡鸦说：“永不再。”

items.meaning: to make or become smaller
items.meaningCN: 减少；减轻（-en 构成动词）
items.example: The medicine lessened the pain within an hour.
items.exampleCN: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

items.meaning: having no end; continuing indefinitely
items.meaningCN: 无休止的；永不完结的（复合形容词）
items.example: The repairs seemed never-ending.
items.exampleCN: 修理工作似乎没完没了。

items.meaning: smaller or less important
items.meaningCN: 较小的；较次要的（比较级形容词）
items.example: They chose the lesser of two risks.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择了两个风险中较小的那个。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 然而；尽管如此（语义平行，非词源）
一点也不少；尽管如此（与 nevertheless 平行的拉丁构式）

entry.definition_en: an accepted standard or pattern of behaviour; the usual level; a mathematical measure of size
entry.core_image: 木匠的曲尺：贴在石面上量出直角，合尺的边才算“正”
entry.scene: Wearing a seatbelt on every trip became the norm by the 1990s.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 norm 是「社会规范／常态」（第 2 个义项：群体共同接受的行为标准）；句意：到 20 世纪 90 年代，每次乘车都系安全带已成为常态。图中可辨识物件：汽车安全带、重复的乘车场景、人群剪影、统计柱状图。

pos.zh: 规范；标准；常态；常模；（数学）范数

derivatives.zh: 使正常化；使规范化；归一化

senses.title: An accepted standard
senses.definition: an accepted standard by which things are judged or measured
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断或衡量事物的公认标准
senses.example: The industry set a norm for safe noise levels.
senses.exampleCN: 该行业为安全噪声水平设定了一个标准。
senses.why: Latin norma was a carpenter's square: a rule laid against a surface to test whether it is true. The first sense is that rule itself, still abstract.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 norma 是木匠的曲尺：贴在表面上检验它是否“正”的规矩。第一个义项就是这把尺子本身，只是已经抽象化。

senses.title: A social norm
senses.definition: a shared expectation about how members of a group should behave
senses.definitionCN: 群体成员对彼此应如何行为的共同期待
senses.example: Wearing a seatbelt on every trip became the norm by the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 到 20 世纪 90 年代，每次乘车都系安全带已成为常态。
senses.why: The same square is now applied to behaviour: the group holds up a measure and expects members to fit it. What fits the square is 'normal'.
senses.whyCN: 同一把曲尺现在用来量行为：群体举起一把尺，期待成员合尺。合尺的就是“正常”。

senses.title: The usual or average level
senses.definition: the usual or average level in a set of data or in ordinary life
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据或日常生活中通常的、平均的水平
senses.example: Rainfall this year is below the norm.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的降雨量低于常态。
senses.why: The rule turns into a measured pattern: what usually happens becomes the line against which exceptions are read. Norm here means 'the usual amount'.
senses.whyCN: 规矩变成了量出来的图案：通常发生的情况成了衡量例外的基准线。这里的 norm 指“通常的量”。

senses.title: A mathematical norm
senses.definition: a function that assigns a size or length to a vector or other mathematical object
senses.definitionCN: 为向量或其他数学对象赋予大小或长度的函数
senses.example: A norm turns a vector into a single non-negative number.
senses.exampleCN: 范数把一个向量变成一个非负实数。
senses.why: The measuring rule becomes a function: norma 'measure' is formalized as a rule that returns the size of an object, not its direction.
senses.whyCN: 量度的规矩变成一个函数：norma“量度”被形式化为一条规则，返回对象的大小而不是方向。

senses.title: A reference-group norm
senses.definition: the standard scores of a reference group used to interpret an individual score
senses.definitionCN: 用来解释个体分数的参照群体标准分数
senses.example: The child's score was compared with the national norm.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子的分数被拿来与全国常模比较。
senses.why: Here the square is supplied by a group: the group's typical performance becomes the ruler against which one person is measured.
senses.whyCN: 这里的曲尺由群体提供：群体的典型表现成了衡量某个人的尺子。

senses.title: Norm-referenced testing
senses.definition: a test interpreted by comparing a candidate with a norm group rather than against a fixed pass mark
senses.definitionCN: 通过把考生与常模群体比较、而非对照固定及格线来解释的测试
senses.example: The exam is norm-referenced, so results are ranked rather than simply passed or failed.
senses.exampleCN: 这场考试是常模参照的，因此结果是排名，而不只是及格或不及格。
senses.why: The compound norm-referenced makes the norm explicit as the reference: each score is placed on the group's scale, and the scale decides what the score means.
senses.whyCN: 复合词 norm-referenced 明确把常模当作参照：每个分数都被放到群体的尺子上，由这把尺子决定分数的含义。

senses.title: A cultural norm
senses.definition: a culturally specific rule about what is proper or expected
senses.definitionCN: 特定文化中关于何为得体、何为应有的规则
senses.example: Every culture has its own norms about personal space.
senses.exampleCN: 每种文化都有自己的个人空间规范。
senses.why: The square is cultural: what counts as 'straight' behaviour differs from group to group, so the same word covers rules that are learned rather than universal.
senses.whyCN: 这把曲尺是文化性的：什么样的行为算“正”，因群体而异，因此同一个词涵盖的是习得而非普世的规则。

senses.title: Departing from the norm
senses.definition: the state of differing from the accepted standard, especially in the phrase depart from the norm
senses.definitionCN: 与公认标准不同的状态，尤用于短语 depart from the norm
senses.example: His working hours depart from the norm for this department.
senses.exampleCN: 他的工作时间偏离了这个部门的常态。
senses.why: Deviation only makes sense against a rule. The norm is the straight line, and 'depart from' names the act of stepping away from it.
senses.whyCN: 偏离只有对照规矩才有意义。norm 是那条直线，“depart from”命名的就是走离这条线的动作。

senses.title: The norm of a vector
senses.definition: a specific measure of a vector's length, such as the Euclidean norm
senses.definitionCN: 对向量长度的具体度量，如欧几里得范数
senses.example: The Euclidean norm of (3, 4) is 5.
senses.exampleCN: 向量 (3, 4) 的欧几里得范数是 5。
senses.why: This is the abstract math norm applied to an arrow: the rule measures how long the arrow is, using the same geometry as a carpenter checking a length.
senses.whyCN: 这是抽象数学范数用在一条箭头上：这条规则量出箭头有多长，用的几何直觉与木匠量长度相同。

intro.en: Norm entered English in 1821 from French norme and Latin norma 'carpenter's square, rule, pattern'. The deeper link to Greek gnomon 'square, indicator' is often suggested but not securely established, so it is marked as uncertain.
intro.cn: norm 于 1821 年经法语 norme 和拉丁语 norma“木匠曲尺、规矩、范式”进入英语。它与希腊语 gnomon“曲尺、标杆”的更深联系常被提及，但并未可靠确立，因此标为存疑。

items.en: First recorded in English as a noun meaning 'a standard, model, or pattern'. It was borrowed from French norme rather than directly from Latin.
items.cn: 1821 年最早记录为英语名词，义为“标准、典范、范式”。它借自法语 norme，而不是直接借自拉丁语。

items.en: norma meant a carpenter's square and, by extension, a rule or standard. The concrete tool comes first: a square tests whether an edge is true, and only later does the word mean an abstract rule.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的曲尺，并引申为规矩或标准。具体的工具在先：曲尺检验一条边是否“正”，后来这个词才表示抽象规则。

items.en: French norme carried the word into English, and English dropped the final vowel of the Latin/French form, giving the bare stem norm. From this stem English builds normal (norm + -al) and normative (norm + -ative).
items.cn: 法语 norme 把词传入英语，英语去掉了拉丁语／法语形式的词尾元音，留下光秃秃的词干 norm。英语从这个词干构成 normal（norm + -al）与 normative（norm + -ative）。

items.en: norma is often connected with Greek gnomon 'carpenter's square, indicator, sundial pin', but the borrowing path is not established. Standard references treat the deeper origin as uncertain; the Greek link should not be presented as fact.
items.cn: norma 常被联系到希腊语 gnomon“曲尺、标杆、日晷指针”，但借入路径并未确立。通行资料把更深来源视为存疑；不应当把希腊语联系当作事实。

items.en: From 'standard' the word develops the statistical sense 'usual amount' in the 19c and the sociological sense 'shared rule of behaviour' in early 20c sociology. The adjective normative is formed to mean 'setting a standard' rather than 'being usual'.
items.cn: 从“标准”出发，这个词在 19 世纪发展出统计义“通常的量”，在 20 世纪初的社会学中发展出“共同行为规则”义。形容词 normative 由此构成，表示“设定标准”而不是“通常如此”。

items.en: In 20c mathematics a norm is a function measuring the size of a vector (normed vector spaces, Banach spaces). In education, norm-referenced testing compares a score with a norm group. Both extend the same 'ruler' image into formal measurement.
items.cn: 在 20 世纪数学中，norm 是量度向量大小的函数（赋范向量空间、巴拿赫空间）。在教育中，常模参照测试把分数与常模群体比较。两者都把同一个“尺子”意象延伸为形式化的测量。

note.en: The first group separates a one-letter neighbour from two derivatives; the second compares words that also name a standard.
note.cn: 第一组区分一个只差一个字母的近邻和两个派生词；第二组比较同样表示“标准”的词。

entries.definition: shape, arrangement, or a printed document. It differs by one letter and comes from Latin forma, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、排列方式或印刷表格。它只差一个字母，来自拉丁语 forma，词根不同。

entries.definition: usual or in line with a standard; formed from norm + -al.
entries.definitionCN: 通常的或合乎标准的；由 norm + -al 构成。

entries.definition: setting or judging by a standard, rather than merely describing what is usual; norm + -ative.
entries.definitionCN: 设定或依据标准的，而不只是描述通常情况；由 norm + -ative 构成。

entries.definition: an accepted level or specification. It is the most general word and can be official or informal.
entries.definitionCN: 公认的水平或规格。它最通用，既可指官方标准，也可指非正式标准。

entries.definition: the typical or middle value of a set of numbers. It is statistical and usually quantitative.
entries.definitionCN: 一组数值中的典型值或中间值。它是统计性的，通常指数量。

entries.definition: a way of doing things that a group has accepted, often without a formal rule.
entries.definitionCN: 群体已接受的做法，往往没有正式规则。

entries.definition: an explicit instruction about what may or must be done. It carries stronger obligation than norm.
entries.definitionCN: 关于可以或必须做什么的明确指示。它比 norm 带有更强的义务性。

entries.definition: a reference point used to compare performance or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 用来比较表现或质量的参照点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real image of the Roman carpenter's square and the real derivatives of the stem.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用罗马木匠曲尺的真实意象，以及这个词干真实的派生词。

normal.en: norma was a carpenter's square: if the edge fits the square, it is 'normal'.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺：边合得上这把尺，就是“正常”的。

normal.en: normal is literally 'according to the norm' — norm + -al.
normal.cn: normal 字面就是“合乎 norm 的”——norm + -al。

normal.en: In statistics the norm is the average line on a graph; data above or below it are deviations.
normal.cn: 统计中，norm 是图上的平均线；高于或低于它的数据就是偏离。

normal.en: In mathematics ||x|| is the norm: one rule turns a whole vector into a length.
normal.cn: 数学中 ||x|| 就是范数：一条规则把整个向量变成一个长度。

normal.en: Social norms are unwritten rules you learn by watching what others expect.
normal.cn: 社会规范是没写下来的规则，你通过观察别人的期待学会它们。

abstract.en: A carpenter lays a square on a stone block and checks whether the corner is true.
abstract.cn: 木匠把曲尺贴在一块石头上，检查那个角是否方正。

abstract.en: A bell curve with a centre line: most cases cluster at the norm, and the tails are the exceptions.
abstract.cn: 一条带中心线的钟形曲线：大多数情况聚集在常态附近，两端是例外。

abstract.en: A ruler laid along an arrow: the norm is the number the ruler reads off.
abstract.cn: 一把尺子沿箭头放好：范数就是尺子读出的那个数。

examples.en: In this office, arriving before nine is the norm.
examples.cn: 在这个办公室，九点前到岗是常态。

examples.en: Every culture has its own norms about personal space.
examples.cn: 每种文化都有自己的个人空间规范。

examples.en: The Euclidean norm of a vector is its straight-line length.
examples.cn: 向量的欧几里得范数就是它的直线长度。
