dict_mnemonic.note: 词源意象记忆 · 非谐音
dict_mnemonic.text: norma 是木匠的曲尺——拿它一量，合尺的边就是“标准”，常见的就是“常态”

entry.root: 拉丁 norma“木匠曲尺、规矩、范式”，核心是“用来量度的标准”；引申为常态、社会规范与数学范数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of norm all come from one tool: a carpenter's square. First it is the rule, then the shared rule, then the usual measure, and finally the mathematical function that measures size.
sensesIntro.cn: norm 的九个义项都来自同一件工具：木匠的曲尺。它先是规矩，再是共同规则，再是通常的度量，最后成为测量大小的数学函数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square laid on a surface to test whether the edge is true.
core.cn: 核心意象：把曲尺贴在表面上，检验这条边是否“正”。

branches.en: RULE AND DEVIATION: the standard is the line, and departing from it is measured against that line.
branches.cn: 规矩与偏离：标准是那条线，偏离就是对照这条线量出来的。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND CULTURAL: a group's shared expectations are the square held up to behaviour.
branches.cn: 社会与文化：群体共同的期待就是举到行为面前的那把曲尺。

branches.en: STATISTICS AND REFERENCE: the usual level and the reference group become the ruler for individuals.
branches.cn: 统计与参照：通常水平和参照群体成为衡量个体的尺子。

branches.en: TESTING: norm-referenced assessment places each score on the group's scale.
branches.cn: 测试：常模参照评价把每个分数放到群体的尺子上。

branches.en: MATHEMATICS: the measuring rule becomes a function returning the size of a vector.
branches.cn: 数学：量度的规矩变成返回向量大小的函数。

intro.en: Norm is a bare Latin stem. English does not add a prefix to it in the basic word; it builds derivatives with -al, -ative, -ity, -ize and -ation, and compounds such as norm-referenced.
intro.cn: norm 是一个光秃秃的拉丁词干。基本词本身不加前缀；英语用 -al、-ative、-ity、-ize、-ation 等后缀构成派生词，并组成 norm-referenced 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is norma 'square, rule', normalis 'according to rule', and enormis 'out of rule' (e- + norma), the source of enormous. The same image of measuring against a rule runs through all of them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 norma“曲尺、规矩”、normalis“合乎规矩的”，以及 enormis“出了规矩的”（e- + norma，enormous 的来源）。同一个“对照规矩来量”的意象贯穿其中。

items.meaning: according to a norm; usual
items.meaningCN: 合乎规范的；通常的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: It is normal to feel nervous before a test.
items.exampleCN: 考试前感到紧张是正常的。

items.meaning: setting or judging by a standard
items.meaningCN: 设定标准的；规范性的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: The study makes a normative claim about how schools should teach.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究对学校应当如何教学提出了规范性主张。

items.meaning: the state of being normal
items.meaningCN: 正常状态；常态（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The city slowly returned to normality after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水过后，城市慢慢恢复正常。

items.meaning: to make normal or bring into a standard form
items.meaningCN: 使正常化；使规范化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The two sides agreed to normalize trade relations.
items.exampleCN: 双方同意使贸易关系正常化。

items.meaning: the act or process of making normal or standard
items.meaningCN: 正常化；规范化；归一化（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: Data normalization makes the measurements comparable.
items.exampleCN: 数据归一化让这些测量值可以相互比较。

items.meaning: lacking norms or standards
items.meaningCN: 没有规范的；缺乏标准的（-less 表示没有）
items.example: A normless society cannot settle disputes predictably.
items.exampleCN: 一个没有规范的社会无法可预测地解决争端。

items.meaning: in a way that sets or appeals to a standard
items.meaningCN: 以规范性的方式；按标准地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The report speaks normatively about what ought to be done.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告以规范性的口吻谈论应当做什么。

items.meaning: interpreted by comparison with a norm group
items.meaningCN: 常模参照的：通过与常模群体比较来解释（复合形容词）
items.example: The test is norm-referenced rather than criterion-referenced.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试是常模参照的，而不是标准参照的。

items.meaning: literally 'out of rule'; hence extremely large
items.meaningCN: 字面“出了规矩的”，因而表示“巨大的”（e- + norm + -ous）
items.example: The storm left an enormous amount of debris.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨留下了大量残骸。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 出了规矩的；不规则的；巨大的

entry.definition_zh: 正常的；通常的；合乎标准的；常态；法线；法向的；师范的（历史义）
entry.definition_en: usual, expected, or in line with a standard; as a noun, the ordinary state, a line at right angles, or a teacher-training institution
entry.core_image: 木匠手里的直角尺：贴着它量出来的那条线，就是“合规矩”的线
entry.scene: Two weeks after the fever, the child's temperature is back to normal and he is playing in the yard again.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 normal 是「正常状态」（第 9 个义项：回到原来的常规水平）；句意：退烧两周后，孩子的体温回到正常，他又在院子里玩了。图中可辨识物件：体温计、院子、跑动的孩子、水杯。

常态；正常水平；（几何）法线；（物理）法向

senses.title: Usual and expected: the ordinary case
senses.definition: happening or existing in the way that is usual for most people or things
senses.definitionCN: 以对大多数人或事物来说通常的方式发生或存在
senses.example: He arrived at his normal time, just after seven.
senses.exampleCN: 他在平常的时间到了，刚过七点。
senses.why: Norma was the carpenter's square, and normalis meant 'made according to the square'. What is measured by the rule is what regularly happens, so 'according to rule' became 'usual'.
senses.whyCN: norma 是木匠的曲尺，normalis 意为“按尺做成的”。用尺量出来的就是按常规会发生的情形，于是“合乎规矩”引申为“通常的”。

senses.title: Conforming to a standard: within the rule
senses.titleCN: 合乎标准的：在规矩之内
senses.definition: matching an accepted standard or reference range, especially in measurement
senses.definitionCN: 符合公认标准或参考范围，尤用于测量
senses.example: The sample is normal for a child of this age.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个年龄的孩子来说，这个样本值是正常的。
senses.why: The suffix -alis makes an adjective meaning 'pertaining to'; normalis is literally 'of the square'. Anything judged by the square falls inside the standard, so the word keeps a measuring sense.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -alis 构成“与……有关的”形容词；normalis 字面就是“属于曲尺的”。凡是用尺量过的东西都在标准之内，因此这个词保留了“测量合规”的义。

senses.title: A normal person: the ordinary member
senses.definition: a person without a medical condition or special status, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 没有疾病或特殊身份的人，作可数名词使用
senses.example: The trial compared normals with patients who had the condition.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验把正常人与此病患者作了比较。
senses.why: The adjective was converted into a noun by dropping the thing it modified. In medicine the 'standard' body becomes a category, and a person inside that category is 'a normal'.
senses.whyCN: 形容词省去所修饰的名词就转成了名词。在医学里，“标准”的身体成了一个类别，落在类别里的人就是 a normal。

senses.title: Normal distribution: the bell-shaped standard curve
senses.titleCN: 正态分布：钟形的标准曲线
senses.definition: the symmetrical probability curve in which most values cluster around the mean
senses.definitionCN: 对称的概率曲线，多数数值聚集在均值附近
senses.example: In a normal distribution, about 68 percent of values lie within one standard deviation.
senses.exampleCN: 在正态分布中，约 68% 的数值落在一个标准差之内。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century statistics borrowed 'normal' to name the curve that was taken as the standard pattern of variation, so the word's 'according to rule' sense was applied to error and measurement.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪统计学借“normal”来命名被视为变异的标准形态的曲线，于是“合乎规矩”这一义被用到误差与测量上。

senses.title: Normal temperature: the healthy baseline
senses.definition: the body temperature regarded as healthy, about 37 degrees Celsius
senses.definitionCN: 被视为健康的体温，约摄氏 37 度
senses.example: Her temperature is back to normal this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今天早上她的体温恢复正常了。
senses.why: Medicine treats the rule-governed reading as the healthy one. What the square says a body should measure becomes the baseline against which illness is a deviation.
senses.whyCN: 医学把“按规矩量出的读数”当作健康值。曲尺规定身体应有的读数，就成了基线；偏离它就是生病。

senses.title: Normal force: the perpendicular push from a surface
senses.titleCN: 法向力：表面垂直方向的推力
senses.definition: the force a surface exerts at right angles to itself on an object touching it
senses.definitionCN: 表面施加在接触物体上、垂直于表面的力
senses.example: The normal force from the floor balances the weight of the box.
senses.exampleCN: 地板对箱子的法向力与箱子的重力平衡。
senses.why: In geometry the 'normal' is the line at right angles to a surface, because a right angle is exactly what the square builds. Physics then names the perpendicular contact force after that line.
senses.whyCN: 几何里的“法线”是垂直于表面的直线，因为直角正是曲尺做出的角。物理学随后用这条线来命名垂直的接触力。

senses.title: The normal: a perpendicular line in geometry
senses.definition: a line or plane that is perpendicular to a given line, curve, or surface at a point
senses.definitionCN: 在某点与给定直线、曲线或曲面垂直的线或面
senses.example: Draw the normal to the curve at point P.
senses.exampleCN: 画出曲线在点 P 处的法线。
senses.why: The noun comes straight from normalis, 'forming a right angle'. The square is the tool that guarantees the right angle, so the line it produces is called the normal.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接来自 normalis“做成直角的”。曲尺正是保证直角的工具，因此由它定出的线就叫 normal。

senses.title: Normal school: a teacher-training college
senses.titleCN: 师范学校：培养教师的学校
senses.definition: a historical term for a college that trained primary school teachers
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指培养小学教师的学院
senses.example: She trained at a normal school before teaching in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 她在师范学校受训，之后到村里教书。
senses.why: The term was borrowed from French école normale, a 'model school' that set the standard for teaching methods. Here 'normal' means 'setting the norm', not 'ordinary'.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法借自法语 école normale，即树立教学法标准的“模范学校”。这里的 normal 是“立规范”，而不是“普通”。

senses.title: Normal state: the previous level restored
senses.definition: the usual condition of a place, system, or person after a disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 地点、系统或人受扰动之后恢复的通常状态
senses.example: The city returned to normal after the storm passed.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，城市恢复了常态。
senses.why: The noun is the adjective standing alone: 'the normal state' loses its noun and keeps the sense of the standard condition. Recovery is simply a return to the line the square draws.
senses.whyCN: 名词是形容词独立使用的结果：“正常状态”省掉了中心词，只留下标准状态之义。所谓恢复，就是回到曲尺画出的那条线。

intro.en: Normal starts as a Latin tool word, not a Latin abstract noun: a carpenter's square becomes an adjective of measurement, and only later a statistical and technical term. Dates for the technical senses are approximate.
intro.cn: normal 的起点是拉丁语里一件工具的称呼，而不是抽象名词：木匠曲尺先变成测量形容词，之后才成为统计与专业术语。专业义项的年代为大致估计。

items.en: Latin norma meant a carpenter's square and, by extension, a rule or pattern. The physical tool is the source of the abstract idea of a standard.
items.cn: 拉丁语 norma 指木匠的曲尺，并引申为规矩、范式。具体的工具是“标准”这一抽象概念的来源。

items.en: The adjective suffix -alis ('pertaining to') was added to norma to make normalis, 'made according to a square, forming a right angle'. This is the first derivation step: noun to adjective.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -alis（“与……有关的”）加在 norma 上，构成 normalis“按曲尺做成的、成直角的”。这是第一级派生：名词变形容词。

items.en: English takes the adjective as normal, first meaning 'typical, according to rule'. The sense has already moved from the tool to conduct: what follows the rule is what usually happens.
items.cn: 英语收入形容词 normal，最初义为“典型的、合乎规则的”。词义已从工具转到行为：合乎规矩的，就是通常发生的。

items.en: The noun normal appears in geometry for the line perpendicular to a curve or surface. No new suffix is added; the adjective's 'right angle' sense is simply used as a noun.
items.cn: 18 世纪几何学中出现名词 normal，指垂直于曲线或曲面的直线。没有再加新后缀，只是把形容词的“直角”义直接名词化。

items.en: Quetelet's 'average man' and later Galton's work give normal distribution its name: the curve treated as the standard pattern of variation. Normal here means 'the norm', not 'ordinary'.
items.cn: 凯特勒的“平均人”及后来高尔顿的工作使 normal distribution 得名：这条曲线被视为变异的标准形态。此处的 normal 是“规范”，而非“普通”。

items.en: normal force and normal school are nineteenth-century extensions, the first from the geometric normal, the second from French école normale. Modern English adds derivatives by ordinary suffixes: normality, normalize, abnormal.
items.cn: normal force 与 normal school 都是 19 世纪的延伸：前者来自几何法线，后者来自法语 école normale。现代英语用普通后缀继续派生：normality、normalize、abnormal。

note.en: Look-alikes are matched by spelling only; near meanings are matched by use. A shared ending does not mean a shared root.
note.cn: “形近”只按拼写配对，“近义”按用法配对。词尾相同并不等于词根相同。

entries.definition: following official or serious conventions. It looks like normal but comes from Latin forma 'shape', not norma.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循正式或严肃的规范。它形似 normal，但来自拉丁语 forma“形状”，而非 norma。

entries.definition: concerned with right and wrong behaviour. The ending matches, but the root is Latin mos (mor-) 'custom'.
entries.definitionCN: 与是非行为有关的。词尾相同，但词根是拉丁语 mos（mor-）“习俗”。

entries.definition: a standard or typical amount. It is the base that normal was built on, not a look-alike with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 标准；典型数量。它是 normal 赖以构成的基础词，不是词根不同的形近词。

entries.definition: happening most often. It describes frequency, while normal also implies 'according to a standard'.
entries.definitionCN: 最常发生的。它讲频率，而 normal 还含“合乎标准”的意思。

entries.definition: not special or unusual. It stresses lack of distinction; normal stresses conformity to expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 不特别、不异常的。它强调“无特殊之处”，normal 强调“符合预期”。

entries.definition: an accepted level used for comparison. It is the measure itself, while normal is what conforms to it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于比较的公认水平。它指标准本身，normal 指符合该标准的状态。

entries.definition: showing the main features of a group. It is about being representative, not about being within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 体现某类主要特征的。它讲代表性，而不讲是否在限度之内。

entries.definition: even, repeated, or following a fixed pattern. It points to rhythm and uniformity rather than a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 均匀的、重复的或按固定规律的。它指向节奏与一致性，而不是规范。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts and real phrases carry the memory; the invented sound hook is kept separate and labelled.
normalIntro.cn: 记忆靠真实构词成分和真实短语；编造的谐音单独放置并明确标注。

normal.en: Norma is a carpenter's square. Every sense of normal is a line measured against that square.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺。normal 的每个义项，都是对着这把尺量出的一条线。

normal.en: The -alis suffix turns the tool into an adjective: normalis means 'of the square', and English keeps that measuring flavour.
normal.cn: 后缀 -alis 把工具变成形容词：normalis 意为“属于曲尺的”，英语保留了这种测量意味。

normal.en: In geometry the normal is the line at right angles, because a right angle is what the square constructs.
normal.cn: 几何里的法线是成直角的那条线，因为直角正是曲尺做出来的。

normal.en: normal distribution is 'the standard curve', not 'the ordinary curve' — the word means the norm.
normal.cn: normal distribution 是“标准曲线”，而不是“普通曲线”——这里的 normal 指规范。

normal.en: A normal school sets the norm for teaching; the French école normale is a model school, not an average one.
normal.cn: normal school 为教学立规范；法语 école normale 是模范学校，不是普通学校。

abstract.en: Picture a square lying on a workbench: the wood is measured, the line is drawn, and 'straight' becomes 'correct'.
abstract.cn: 想象工作台上放着一把曲尺：木头被量过，线被画出，“直”就变成了“对”。

abstract.en: From one right angle grow two families: the measuring family (standard, temperature) and the geometric family (normal line, normal force).
abstract.cn: 从一个直角长出两族含义：测量族（标准、体温）与几何族（法线、法向力）。

abstract.en: The same word then jumps from the workshop to the statistician's table and to the teacher's college, still carrying 'according to the norm'.
abstract.cn: 同一个词又从工坊跳到统计学家的桌面和师范学院的讲台，始终带着“合乎规范”的意思。

examples.en: Under normal circumstances the train takes forty minutes.
examples.cn: 在正常情况下，这趟火车要走四十分钟。

examples.en: The doctor said the scan was normal and no treatment was needed.
examples.cn: 医生说扫描结果正常，不需要治疗。

examples.en: Life slowly returned to normal after the factory reopened.
examples.cn: 工厂重新开工后，生活慢慢恢复常态。

dict_mnemonic.text: “诺曼”——诺曼人做事讲规矩，样样都要量成 normal（正常、标准）

entry.root: 拉丁 norma“曲尺、规矩”+ -alis 形容词后缀 → normalis“按尺做成的、成直角的” → “合乎规矩的、标准的、常态的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of normal radiate from one object, the carpenter's square: a measured line is a standard, a standard is what usually happens, and a right angle is what geometry calls the normal.
sensesIntro.cn: normal 的九个义项都从一件东西辐射出来——木匠的曲尺：量出的线是标准，标准就是通常发生的情形，而直角正是几何所说的法线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter's square on a workbench — the line drawn against it is 'correct'.
core.cn: 核心意象：工作台上的木匠曲尺——贴着它画出的线就是“正确的”。

branches.en: MEASURED BY THE RULE: what conforms to the square is both usual and within standard.
branches.cn: 按尺衡量：合乎曲尺的，既属通常，也在标准之内。

branches.en: THE NORMAL BODY AND STATE: a healthy reading, a person inside the category, and a condition restored.
branches.cn: 正常身体与状态：健康的读数、落在类别中的人，以及恢复了的状况。

branches.en: THE STATISTICAL NORM: the bell curve named as the standard pattern of variation.
branches.cn: 统计规范：以标准变异形态命名的钟形曲线。

branches.en: RIGHT ANGLE IN SPACE: the perpendicular line and the force along it.
branches.cn: 空间中的直角：垂直线以及沿该线的力。

branches.en: SETTING THE NORM: the normal school is a model school, where normal means 'norm-giving'.
branches.cn: 树立规范：normal school 是模范学校，此处 normal 意为“立规范的”。

intro.en: Normal is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective suffix; English then adds its own endings. The base norm is now felt as a separate word, so the family splits into norm- words and normal- words.
intro.cn: normal 是拉丁名词加拉丁形容词后缀，英语随后再加自己的词尾。基础词 norm 现在被视为独立单词，因此这个词族分成 norm- 系与 normal- 系。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma and normalis are both attested; abnormis 'irregular' shows the same base with ab-. Later Latin also forms normativus, the source of normative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma 与 normalis 均有文献可证；abnormis“不规则的”显示同一词基加 ab-。晚期拉丁语还有 normativus，是 normative 的来源。

items.meaning: according to a standard; usual
items.meaningCN: 合乎标准的；通常的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: This is a normal response to stress.
items.exampleCN: 这是对压力的正常反应。

items.meaning: usually; in the normal way
items.meaningCN: 通常；正常情况下（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The office normally opens at nine.
items.exampleCN: 办公室通常九点开门。

items.meaning: the state of being normal
items.meaningCN: 正常状态；常态（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The return to normality took months.
items.exampleCN: 恢复正常用了好几个月。

items.meaning: to make normal or bring to a standard scale
items.meaningCN: 使正常化；使标准化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The software normalizes the data before comparison.
items.exampleCN: 软件在比较前先把数据归一化。

items.meaning: the process of making something normal or standard
items.meaningCN: 正常化；标准化的过程（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Normalization of the two databases took a week.
items.exampleCN: 两个数据库的归一化花了一周。

items.meaning: departing from the standard; unusual in a worrying way
items.meaningCN: 偏离标准的；异常的（ab- 表示“离开”）
items.example: The test showed an abnormal heart rhythm.
items.exampleCN: 检查显示心律异常。

items.meaning: a standard, rule, or typical amount
items.meaningCN: 规范；准则；典型量（由 normal 反推的基础词）
items.example: Working from home became the norm.
items.exampleCN: 居家办公成了常态。

items.meaning: setting or judging by a standard
items.meaningCN: 规范性的；立标准的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: The paper makes a normative claim about fairness.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文对公平提出了规范性主张。

latinEntries.meaning: made to a square; forming a right angle
latinEntries.meaningCN: 按曲尺做成的；成直角的
用以立标准的（晚期拉丁语）

entry.definition_zh: 概念；想法；观念；看法；一时念头；（复数，美式）缝纫小配件
entry.definition_en: an idea, belief, or conception in the mind; in the plural in American English, small sewing supplies
entry.core_image: 脑海里亮起的一团轮廓：还没有形状，却已经被认出来
entry.scene: On the whiteboard she sketched her notion of a garden that could feed a whole street.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 notion 是「构想、概念」（第 1 个义项：头脑中的想法）；句意：她在白板上勾勒出自己关于“能养活整条街的菜园”的构想。图中可辨识物件：白板、草图、菜畦、街道。

pos.zh: 概念；想法；观念；看法
一时念头；奇想
（复数 notions，美式）缝纫小配件；小百货

derivatives.zh: 注意；通知（同族词，非直接派生）
臭名昭著的（同族词，经“众所周知”义转贬）

senses.title: A concept or idea in the mind
senses.definition: an idea or conception that exists in someone's mind, especially one that is not yet concrete
senses.definitionCN: 存在于某人头脑中的想法或构想，尤指尚未具体化者
senses.example: The notion of justice is easier to feel than to define.
senses.exampleCN: 正义这个概念，感受起来比下定义容易。
senses.why: Latin notio is 'a knowing', built from noscere 'to come to know' plus the noun suffix -tio. The suffix turns the act of knowing into its result: what has been grasped in the mind is a notion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notio 意为“一次知晓”，由 noscere“认识”加名词后缀 -tio 构成。该后缀把“认识”这个动作变成其结果：心里把握住的东西，就是 notion。

senses.title: A belief or opinion held about something
senses.definition: a belief or view that a person holds, often without full proof
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所持的信念或观点，常无充分证据
senses.example: He has some odd notions about what makes a healthy diet.
senses.exampleCN: 他对什么算健康饮食有些古怪的看法。
senses.why: The -tio noun can name not only a concept but a concept accepted as true. What the mind has grasped is then treated as fact, and notion shifts from 'idea' to 'opinion'.
senses.whyCN: -tio 名词不仅能指概念，也能指被当作真而接受的概念。心里把握住的东西被当成事实，notion 就从“想法”滑向“看法”。

senses.title: A sudden whim or fancy
senses.definition: a sudden desire or idea with little reason behind it
senses.definitionCN: 突然出现、缺少理由的念头或欲望
senses.example: She had a sudden notion to paint the front door green.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然起念，要把前门刷成绿色。
senses.why: In the seventeenth century notion acquired the sense of a thought that simply appears. Since a notion is only in the mind, it can be a thought with nothing behind it, and 'idea' becomes 'whim'.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 notion 获得“凭空出现的念头”义。既然 notion 只在心里，它就可以是背后空无一物的念头，“想法”于是变成“奇想”。

senses.title: Notions: small sewing supplies
senses.definition: in American English, the plural means small items used in sewing, such as thread, buttons, and pins
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中复数指缝纫用的小物件，如线、纽扣、别针
senses.example: The shop sells thread, buttons, and other sewing notions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖线、纽扣和其他缝纫小配件。
senses.why: This is a separate American extension of the plural: 'notions' came to mean small useful articles, then specifically sewing items. The link to 'idea' is weak, and the origin of this sense is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 这是复数在美式英语中的独立延伸：notions 先指有用的小物件，再专指缝纫用品。它与“想法”的联系很弱，这一义项的来源存疑。

senses.title: One's conception of what something should be
senses.definition: the standard or conception a person holds about a role, duty, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对某种角色、责任或品质所持的标准或观念
senses.example: He has a very high notion of what a doctor owes a patient.
senses.exampleCN: 他对医生应尽之责有着很高的标准。
senses.why: The pattern notion of X names the concept someone carries about X. Because the concept sets an expectation, 'a high notion of duty' means a demanding standard, not merely an idea.
senses.whyCN: notion of X 这一结构指某人心里对 X 所抱的概念。概念会立出预期，所以 a high notion of duty 指要求很高的标准，而不只是一个想法。

senses.title: The notion that: a proposition treated as an idea
senses.titleCN: the notion that：作为一个观念来看的命题
senses.definition: used with a clause to present a belief as a claim that can be examined or rejected
senses.definitionCN: 后接从句，把一种信念作为可被检验或否定的主张提出来
senses.example: The notion that money buys happiness is widely questioned.
senses.exampleCN: “金钱能买到幸福”这一观念受到广泛质疑。
senses.why: The noun takes a full clause as its content, so the concept is stated as a proposition. The -tio noun still means 'what is known or thought', but the content is now a whole sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词以完整从句作内容，于是概念被陈述为一个命题。-tio 名词仍表示“所认识或所想到的内容”，只是内容变成了整句话。

senses.title: An abstract conception without a physical object
senses.titleCN: 无具体对象的抽象概念
senses.definition: a purely mental conception, such as infinity or number, that has no concrete referent
senses.definitionCN: 纯粹的心智概念，如无穷或数，没有具体所指
senses.example: Infinity is an abstract notion that children grasp late.
senses.exampleCN: 无穷是一个儿童较晚才能掌握的抽象概念。
senses.why: Here the word is closest to notio as a pure act of understanding: nothing in the world is pointed at, and the notion exists only as something known.
senses.whyCN: 此处最接近 notio 作为纯粹理解行为的本义：并不指向世上的任何东西，notion 只作为“被认识之物”存在。

senses.title: A vague or slight understanding
senses.definition: in phrases such as have no notion, a minimal degree of knowledge about something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 have no notion 等短语，表示对某事的了解极少
senses.example: I have no notion how this machine actually works.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全不知道这台机器究竟怎么运作。
senses.why: This sense preserves the original verb idea of knowing. 'No notion' is literally 'no knowing', so the noun measures knowledge rather than naming a concept.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留了最初“知道”的动词意味。no notion 字面就是“没有知晓”，所以这个名词是在衡量知识多少，而不是命名一个概念。

senses.title: A widely shared popular idea
senses.definition: an idea current among many people, often one that is repeated rather than tested
senses.definitionCN: 在许多人中间流传的观念，常被重复而未经检验
senses.example: The popular notion that we use only ten percent of our brains is false.
senses.exampleCN: “我们只用了大脑的百分之十”这一流行观念是错误的。
senses.why: A notion can belong to a group rather than an individual. Once the -tio noun is shared, it becomes a current idea, and the adjective popular simply marks how far it has spread.
senses.whyCN: notion 可以不属个人而属群体。当这个 -tio 名词被共享，它就成了流行观念，形容词 popular 只是标明它传播得多广。

intro.en: Notion is a Latin noun of knowing. The chain is verb to participle to abstract noun; whether English took it straight from Latin or through French is not fully settled, and the sewing sense is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: notion 是一个表示“知晓”的拉丁名词。链条是动词→分词→抽象名词；英语是直接从拉丁语借入还是经法语中转，尚无定论；缝纫义项的来源也不确定。

items.en: The verb noscere (also gnoscere) meant 'to come to know, learn'. Its -sc- form is inceptive, marking the entry into a state of knowing rather than knowledge already held.
items.cn: 动词 noscere（亦作 gnoscere）意为“逐渐认识、得知”。其 -sc- 形式表起始，强调进入“知道”的状态，而非已拥有知识。

items.en: The past participle notus 'known' supplies the stem not-. This is the step from verb to adjective: what has been learned is 'known'.
items.cn: 过去分词 notus“已知的”提供词干 not-。这是从动词到形容词的一步：被学到的东西就是“已知的”。

items.en: Adding -tio (action or result noun) to the stem gives notio 'a knowing, concept, idea'. The suffix converts the act of knowing into a thing that can be discussed.
items.cn: 词干加 -tio（行为或结果名词后缀）得到 notio“知晓、概念、想法”。该后缀把“认识”这一动作转化成可以谈论的“东西”。

items.en: English records notion in the late fourteenth century meaning 'understanding, concept'. A route through Old French is often assumed but not certain, so the transmission path is marked 存疑.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪晚期记录 notion，义为“理解、概念”。通常假定经古法语传入，但并不确定，故传播路径标注为存疑。

items.en: The sense widens from 'concept' to 'opinion, belief' in the sixteenth century, then to 'a whim' in the seventeenth. The same noun now names both a grasped idea and a groundless one.
items.cn: 16 世纪词义从“概念”扩展到“看法、信念”，17 世纪再扩展到“一时奇想”。同一个名词既指把握住的观念，也指毫无根据的念头。

items.en: American English develops the plural notions for small sewing articles in the nineteenth century; its origin is uncertain. Modern English fixes the patterns the notion that and have no notion of.
items.cn: 美式英语在 19 世纪发展出复数 notions 表示缝纫小配件，其来源不确定。现代英语固定了 the notion that 与 have no notion of 等结构。

note.en: Spelling neighbours are grouped first because notion's Latin neighbours look alike but split into different roots; meaning neighbours come second.
note.cn: 先列形近词，因为 notion 的拉丁邻居外形相似却分属不同词根；再列近义词。

entries.definition: a country and its people. It ends like notion but comes from nasci 'to be born', not from knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 国家及其人民。词尾像 notion，但来自 nasci“出生”，与“知道”无关。

entries.definition: a system of written symbols. It comes from notare 'to mark', a different verb from noscere.
entries.definitionCN: 书写符号系统。它来自 notare“标记”，与 noscere 是不同动词。

entries.definition: existing only in theory or name. It is the adjective from notion, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 仅存在于理论或名义上的。它是 notion 派生的形容词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a thought or plan in the mind. It is the broad everyday word, while notion often sounds slightly abstract or tentative.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中的想法或计划。它是最宽泛的日常词，而 notion 常显得略抽象或不确定。

entries.definition: a general idea formed by grouping things. It is more technical and more sharply defined than notion.
entries.definitionCN: 通过归类事物形成的一般观念。它比 notion 更专业，边界也更清晰。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is true. It stresses acceptance, while notion stresses the content held in mind.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事为真的感觉。它强调接受，而 notion 强调心中所持的内容。

entries.definition: an unformed opinion based on first contact. It is vaguer and more momentary than notion.
entries.definitionCN: 基于初次接触而形成的不成形看法。它比 notion 更模糊、更短暂。

entries.definition: a sudden wish with no strong reason. It matches the third sense of notion but is always about desire.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏坚实理由的突发愿望。它对应 notion 的第 3 个义项，但总与欲望有关。

normalIntro.en: The memory hooks below use the real Latin family: noscere, notus, notio, and their English descendants. Nothing here is invented etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词族：noscere、notus、notio 及其英语后代。此处没有编造词源。

normal.en: noscere means 'to come to know'; notus means 'known'; notio is 'a knowing'. Notion is the thing that results when you know.
normal.cn: noscere 意为“逐渐认识”；notus 意为“已知的”；notio 是“一次知晓”。notion 就是你“知道”之后留在心里的那个东西。

normal.en: The -tio suffix is the same one behind nation, action and creation: it turns an act into a result you can name.
normal.cn: -tio 这个后缀也出现在 nation、action、creation 中：它把动作变成可以命名的结果。

normal.en: Same family, different routes: notice and notify both go back to notus, while noble goes back to gnobilis 'knowable' and drifted to 'well known, high-born'.
normal.cn: 同族不同路：notice 与 notify 都回到 notus，而 noble 回到 gnobilis“可知的”，再漂移为“众所周知的、出身高贵的”。

normal.en: have no notion of = 'have no knowing of'. The phrase keeps the oldest, verb-like sense of the noun.
normal.cn: have no notion of =“对……没有知晓”。这个短语保留了该名词最古老、最接近动词的义。

normal.en: Because a notion lives only in the mind, it can be a solid concept or an empty whim; the word does not tell you which.
normal.cn: 因为 notion 只存在于心里，它既可以是扎实的概念，也可以是空泛的奇想；这个词本身不告诉你是哪一种。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switched on in a dark room: first there is no knowing, then a shape appears. Notion is that shape before it is named.
abstract.cn: 想象黑屋里一盏灯亮起：先是“不知道”，然后一个轮廓出现。notion 就是被命名之前的那团轮廓。

abstract.en: The same shape can be shared by a whole crowd, and then it becomes a popular notion — still just a shape, not proof.
abstract.cn: 同一团轮廓可以被一群人共享，于是成了 popular notion——仍然只是轮廓，不是证据。

abstract.en: The word's history is a widening circle: knowing, then concept, then opinion, then whim, then a small item on a sewing table.
abstract.cn: 这个词的历史是一圈圈扩大的：知道→概念→看法→奇想→缝纫桌上的小物件。

examples.en: The notion that the earth was flat persisted for centuries.
examples.cn: “地球是平的”这一观念延续了好几个世纪。

examples.en: She rejected the notion of working for anyone else.
examples.cn: 她拒绝了为任何人打工的想法。

examples.en: I had no notion of how much the repairs would cost.
examples.cn: 我完全不知道修理要花多少钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: “NO 神”——心里说“没有神”，这只是一个 notion（想法、观念），还没被证明

entry.root: 拉丁 noscere“认识、得知”→ 分词 notus“已知的”+ -tio 名词后缀 → notio“知晓、概念、想法”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one line: the -tio noun starts as 'a knowing', becomes 'a concept', then 'an opinion', then 'a whim', and finally splits into a shared idea and an American sewing term.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着一条线展开：这个 -tio 名词从“一次知晓”起步，变成“概念”，再变成“看法”，再变成“奇想”，最后分出“共享观念”和美式缝纫用语两支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape lights up in the mind — something known before it has a name.
core.cn: 核心意象：心里亮起一团轮廓——在拥有名字之前就已被认识的东西。

branches.en: PURE CONCEPTION: from a grasped idea to an abstract notion such as infinity, the -tio noun names what the mind holds.
branches.cn: 纯粹概念：从把握住的想到无穷这类抽象概念，这个 -tio 名词命名心里所持之物。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT AND PROPOSITION: a notion can be believed, held as a standard, or stated as a that-clause.
branches.cn: 判断与命题：notion 可以被相信、被当作标准，也可以用 that 从句陈述。

branches.en: GROUNDLESS THOUGHT: because the idea lives only in the mind, it can appear with nothing behind it and become a whim.
branches.cn: 无据之念：因为想法只存在于心里，它可以凭空出现、背后无物，于是成为奇想。

branches.en: KNOWING ITSELF: have no notion keeps the oldest sense, where the noun still measures knowledge.
branches.cn: 知晓本身：have no notion 保留最古老的义，名词仍在衡量“知道”的多少。

branches.en: FROM MIND TO MARKET: a notion shared by many becomes popular opinion; the American plural turns into small goods on a counter.
branches.cn: 从心智到市场：被众人共享的 notion 成为流行观念；美式复数则变成柜台上的小商品。

intro.en: Notion itself is stem plus suffix; English adds -al and -ly to build the adjective and adverb. The wider family is Latin know- words that reached English by different routes.
intro.cn: notion 本身是词干加后缀；英语再加 -al 与 -ly 构成形容词和副词。更大的词族是经由不同路径进入英语的拉丁“知”系词。

latinIntro.en: Latin notio, notus and noscere are all attested, and notitia gives English notice. The gn- spellings belong to the older layer of the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 notio、notus、noscere 均有文献可证，notitia 则给出英语 notice。带 gn- 的拼写属于同一动词的更古老层次。

items.meaning: a concept or idea held in the mind
items.meaningCN: 心中所持的概念或想法（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The notion of zero took a long time to reach Europe.
items.exampleCN: 零的概念花了很长时间才传到欧洲。

items.meaning: existing in concept rather than in fact
items.meaningCN: 概念上的；非实际的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The cost is notional and never appears on a bill.
items.exampleCN: 这项费用只是名义上的，从不出现在账单上。

items.meaning: in theory or in name only
items.meaningCN: 在理论上；名义上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The land is notionally divided among the heirs.
items.exampleCN: 这块地在名义上分给了各位继承人。

items.meaning: attention, or a warning given to someone
items.meaningCN: 注意；通知（经拉丁 notitia“知识”而来）
items.example: He took no notice of the sign.
items.exampleCN: 他没注意那块标牌。

items.meaning: to make someone know; to inform officially
items.meaningCN: 使某人知道；正式通知（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: Please notify the office of any change of address.
items.exampleCN: 地址如有变动，请通知办公室。

items.meaning: an official message that makes someone aware
items.meaningCN: 通知；告知信息（-ication 构成过程名词）
items.example: A notification appeared on the screen.
items.exampleCN: 屏幕上出现了一条通知。

items.meaning: the mental process of knowing
items.meaningCN: 认知；认识过程（co- + gnosc- + -ition）
items.example: Sleep affects memory and cognition.
items.exampleCN: 睡眠影响记忆与认知。

items.meaning: to know again; to identify as previously seen
items.meaningCN: 认出；识别（re-“再”+ cogn-“知”+ -ize）
items.example: I did not recognize him in the old photograph.
items.exampleCN: 在那张旧照片里我没认出他。

items.meaning: of high rank or fine character
items.meaningCN: 高贵的；品格高尚的（由“可知的”转为“众所周知的、出身高贵的”）
items.example: She made a noble attempt to save the village school.
items.exampleCN: 她为保住村校做了一次高尚的尝试。

items.meaning: to add notes or marks to a text
items.meaningCN: 给文本加注（ad- + nota“标记”+ -ate；注意此词根是 notare，非 noscere）
items.example: Students annotate the poem in the margins.
items.exampleCN: 学生们在页边给这首诗加注。

entry.definition_zh: 客观的；无偏见的；基于事实的；目标的；宾格的；物镜（名词）
entry.definition_en: based on observable facts rather than personal feelings; as a noun, a goal, the accusative case, or the lens nearest the specimen in a microscope
entry.core_image: 把某物从自己面前推出去、摆到对面：它因此不再属于“我”的视角
entry.scene: The auditor laid the invoices on the table and judged the accounts by the documents alone, keeping her objective stance throughout.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 objective 是「客观无偏的」（第 1 个义项：不受个人情感影响的）；句意：审计员把发票摊在桌上，只凭文件判断账目，全程保持客观立场。图中可辨识物件：发票、账本、桌面、签字笔。

pos.zh: 客观的；无偏见的；基于事实的；宾格的（语法）
目标；目的；（显微镜）物镜

forms.label: 复数（名词，多于一个目标）

derivatives.zh: 物体；对象；反对（同根基础词）
主观性（对应词，sub- 相反方向）

senses.title: Impartial: not swayed by personal feeling
senses.titleCN: 客观无偏：不受个人情感左右
senses.definition: judging or observing without letting personal feelings, interests, or bias affect the result
senses.definitionCN: 判断或观察时不让个人情感、利益或偏见影响结果
senses.example: A judge must stay objective even when the case is emotionally charged.
senses.exampleCN: 即使案件牵动情绪，法官也必须保持客观。
senses.why: Objectum is 'what is thrown before you', from ob- 'toward, against' plus jacere 'to throw'. To be objective is to put the thing in front of you and look at it from outside your own feelings.
senses.whyCN: objectum 是“被扔到你面前之物”，由 ob-“朝向、对着”加 jacere“投掷”构成。所谓客观，就是把事物摆到自己面前，从个人情感之外看它。

senses.title: Based on observable facts and data
senses.titleCN: 基于可观察的事实与数据
senses.definition: resting on evidence that can be measured, checked, or repeated by others
senses.definitionCN: 建立在他人可测量、可核查或可重复的证据之上
senses.example: The report relies on objective data rather than on anecdote.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告依据客观数据，而不是轶事。
senses.why: If the object is thrown before everyone, it is public rather than private. Facts that all observers can check are therefore 'objective', and the word shifts from attitude to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 如果客体被扔到所有人面前，它就是公共的而非私人的。所有观察者都能核查的事实因而是“客观的”，词义也从态度转向证据。

senses.title: A goal or aim to be reached
senses.definition: a specific result that a plan, project, or military operation is intended to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 计划、项目或军事行动意图达到的具体结果
senses.example: The main objective of the study is to test the new drug.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究的主要目标是检验这种新药。
senses.why: The noun sense comes from the 'object before the mind' idea: a goal is what you set in front of you and move toward. Military usage in the late nineteenth century fixed 'objective' as a target.
senses.whyCN: 名词义来自“摆在心前的对象”：目标就是你放到面前、朝它前进的东西。19 世纪晚期的军事用法把 objective 固定为“攻击目标”。

senses.title: The objective case: the grammatical object form
senses.titleCN: 宾格：语法中的宾语形式
senses.definition: the case form of a pronoun or noun when it functions as a verb's object, as in him or me
senses.definitionCN: 代词或名词作动词宾语时的格形式，如 him、me
senses.example: In 'she saw him', 'him' is in the objective case.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she saw him 中，him 是宾格。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the word because the case marks the object of the verb. The 'object' is again what is thrown before the action, so the form that marks it is called objective.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，因为该格标记动词的宾语。宾语仍是“被置于动作之前的东西”，标记它的形式就叫宾格。

senses.title: The objective lens of a microscope
senses.definition: the lens closest to the specimen, which forms the first image in a microscope
senses.definitionCN: 显微镜中最靠近标本、形成第一幅像的透镜
senses.example: Switch to the 40x objective for a closer look.
senses.exampleCN: 换到 40 倍物镜看得更近。
senses.why: In optics the objective is the lens that faces the object. The adjective's 'pertaining to the object' sense is simply used as a noun, naming the lens nearest the thing observed.
senses.whyCN: 光学中 objective 是正对物体的那块透镜。形容词“与客体有关的”义直接名词化，用来命名最靠近被观察物的镜片。

senses.title: Objective reality: what exists apart from the mind
senses.titleCN: 客观现实：独立于心灵而存在的东西
senses.definition: in philosophy, reality that exists independently of anyone's perception or belief
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指不依赖任何人的感知或信念而存在的现实
senses.example: The debate asks whether an objective reality exists beyond our perceptions.
senses.exampleCN: 争论在于：我们的感知之外是否存在着客观现实。
senses.why: Philosophy split the world into subject and object, and objectivus marked whatever belongs to the object side. Reality on that side is objective because it does not depend on the observer.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把世界分为主体与客体，objectivus 标记属于客体一侧的东西。客体一侧的现实之所以是“客观的”，因为它不依赖观察者。

senses.title: An objective test: one scored without judgement
senses.titleCN: 客观测试：不依赖评分者判断的测验
senses.definition: a test, usually multiple-choice, whose answers can be marked the same way by any scorer
senses.definitionCN: 通常为选择题的测验，任何评分者都能以同样方式判分
senses.example: An objective test can be scored by a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 客观测试可以由机器评分。
senses.why: The word is applied to scoring rather than to things: a test is objective when the marker's personal view cannot enter. Again the answer sits outside the judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被用到评分上，而不是事物上：当评分者的个人看法无法进入时，测试就是 objective。答案再次被置于评判者之外。

senses.title: The objective function in optimization
senses.definition: the mathematical function that an algorithm tries to minimize or maximize
senses.definitionCN: 算法试图最小化或最大化的那个数学函数
senses.example: The algorithm adjusts the weights to minimize the objective function.
senses.exampleCN: 算法调整权重以最小化目标函数。
senses.why: Mathematics keeps the goal sense and makes it precise: the function is the formal object the search is directed at, so it is called the objective function.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留“目标”义并使之精确：该函数就是搜索所指向的形式化对象，因此称为目标函数。

senses.title: Objective evidence: proof independent of testimony
senses.titleCN: 客观证据：不依赖陈述的证明
senses.definition: evidence such as physical traces or measurements that does not depend on a witness's account
senses.definitionCN: 如物证或测量数据之类、不依赖证人陈述的证据
senses.example: There is no objective evidence linking him to the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 没有客观证据把他与现场联系起来。
senses.why: Evidence is objective when it stands in front of the court as a thing, rather than inside a witness's mind. The ob- 'before' in the root is felt almost literally here.
senses.whyCN: 当证据作为“物”摆在法庭面前、而不是留在证人心里时，它就是客观的。词根中 ob-“在前”在这里几乎被字面地感受到。

intro.en: Objective is a medieval Latin philosophical adjective built on the past participle of obicere, 'to throw before'. Its modern sense is surprisingly recent, and the seventeenth-century sense was almost the reverse.
intro.cn: objective 是中世纪拉丁语的哲学形容词，建立在 obicere“扔到前面”的过去分词之上。它的现代义项出现得相当晚，而 17 世纪的用法几乎相反。

items.en: obicere = ob- 'toward, against, in front of' + jacere 'to throw'. Literally 'to throw something in front of someone', hence 'to put before, expose, oppose'.
items.cn: obicere = ob-“朝向、对着、在前”+ jacere“投掷”，字面为“把某物扔到某人面前”，故有“置于前、呈现、对抗”之义。

items.en: Its past participle objectum was used as a noun for 'that which is thrown before the mind or senses'. This is the base noun object: the thing standing over against the knower.
items.cn: 其过去分词 objectum 作名词，指“被置于心智或感官之前的东西”。这就是基础名词 object：立在认识者对面的物。

items.en: Scholastic Latin formed objectivus 'relating to an object of thought'. In seventeenth-century usage an 'objective' quality could mean one existing in the mind as an object of thought, which is close to the opposite of today's sense.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语构成 objectivus“与思想对象有关的”。在 17 世纪用法中，objective 的性质可指“作为思想对象存在于心中的”，这与今天的义几乎相反。

items.en: English adopts the adjective in the 1610s as a philosophical term. It describes what belongs to the object side of experience rather than to the thinking subject.
items.cn: 英语在 1610 年代收入该形容词，作为哲学术语，描述属于经验中客体一侧、而非思维主体一侧的东西。

items.en: The sense 'unbiased, dealing with things as they are apart from personal view' is dated to about 1855. It grows out of the subject/object split: to be objective is to take the object's side.
items.cn: “无偏见、按事物本来面目处理而不掺个人看法”这一义项约始于 1855 年。它从主客二分中生长出来：客观就是站到客体那一边。

items.en: The noun 'goal' is dated to 1881, from the military sense of a target to be reached. Technical uses follow: the objective lens in optics, the objective case in grammar, the objective test and objective function in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 名词“目标”约始于 1881 年，来自军事上要抵达的目标。技术用法随后展开：光学的物镜、语法的宾格，以及 20 世纪的客观测试与目标函数。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ject- root but differs in prefix; the near-meaning group differs in what is being praised or measured.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ject- 词根而前缀不同；近义组的差别在于所称赞或所衡量的对象不同。

entries.definition: based on personal feeling rather than external facts. It uses sub- 'under' instead of ob- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 基于个人感受而非外部事实的。它用 sub-“在下”而非 ob-“在前”。

entries.definition: a statement of disagreement. It is object + -ion, literally 'a throwing against'.
entries.definitionCN: 反对意见。它是 object + -ion，字面为“对着扔过去”。

entries.definition: a thing that can be seen or touched; also the verb 'to oppose'. It is the noun and verb that objective was built on.
entries.definitionCN: 可见可触之物；亦作动词“反对”。它是 objective 赖以构成的名词与动词。

entries.definition: not favouring one side over another. It is about fairness between parties; objective is about keeping feeling out of judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方。它讲双方之间的公平，objective 讲把情感排除在判断之外。

entries.definition: free from preconceived prejudice. It is narrower and more personal than objective.
entries.definitionCN: 没有先入之见的。它比 objective 更窄，也更指向个人态度。

entries.definition: concerned with facts that can be checked. It describes content, while objective describes the stance behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 以可核查的事实为内容的。它描述内容，objective 描述背后的立场。

entries.definition: the result a person or plan aims at. It matches the noun objective but is more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或计划所瞄准的结果。它对应名词 objective，但更日常。

entries.definition: a purpose or intention. It is softer and less formal than objective.
entries.definitionCN: 目的或意图。它比 objective 更柔和、更不正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below follow the real morphemes ob- and ject-, and the real historical reversal of the philosophical sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子依据真实语素 ob- 与 ject-，以及哲学义项真实的历史反转。

normal.en: ob- 'before' + jacere 'throw' = 'throw in front of'. An object is what you throw down in front of you and then look at.
normal.cn: ob-“在前”+ jacere“扔”=“扔到面前”。客体就是你扔到自己面前、然后加以观看的东西。

normal.en: Object, objection, objective, subject, project, reject: one ject- root, different prefixes showing direction.
normal.cn: object、objection、objective、subject、project、reject：一个 ject- 词根，不同前缀表示不同方向。

normal.en: Being objective is standing on the object's side of the subject/object line; being subjective is standing on the subject's side.
normal.cn: 客观就是站在主客二分中客体那一边；主观就是站在主体那一边。

normal.en: The 1610s adjective meant 'existing as an object of thought', nearly the reverse of today; the modern 'unbiased' sense is only 1855.
normal.cn: 1610 年代的形容词意为“作为思想对象而存在”，与今天几乎相反；现代“无偏见”义不过始于 1855 年。

normal.en: A microscope objective faces the object; a military objective is the thing ahead that you move toward.
normal.cn: 显微镜物镜正对着被观察物；军事目标是你朝之前进的那个东西。

abstract.en: Picture both hands pushing a box away from your chest and setting it on the far side of a table: that distance is objectivity.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把一只箱子从胸前推开、放到桌子对面：这段距离就是客观。

abstract.en: The same gesture produces the noun and the adjective: the box is the objective, the far-side view is objective.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作产生名词与形容词：箱子是 objective（目标/客体），从对面看就是 objective（客观的）。

abstract.en: Optics, grammar, statistics and philosophy all name their 'thing on the far side' with this one word.
abstract.cn: 光学、语法、统计与哲学，都用这同一个词来命名各自“对面那个东西”。

examples.en: Try to give an objective account of what happened.
examples.cn: 试着对发生的事给出客观的叙述。

examples.en: Our objective is to cut delivery time by half.
examples.cn: 我们的目标是把交付时间缩短一半。

examples.en: The reviewer questioned whether the study was truly objective.
examples.cn: 评审人质疑这项研究是否真正客观。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，不接题”——不接自己的主观题，只按事实打分 → objective 客观的；另外把“目标”想成摆在正前方的靶子

entry.root: 拉丁 ob-“在前、对着”+ jacere“投掷”→ objectum“被扔到面前之物”+ -ive 形容词后缀 → objective“属于客体一侧的、客观的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all rest on one spatial move: something is thrown in front of you and viewed from the far side. Feeling, fact, goal, case, lens and proof are all 'objects' on that far side.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都建立在同一个空间动作上：某物被扔到你面前，并从对面被观看。情感、事实、目标、格、镜片与证据，都是对面那一侧的“客体”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing placed on the far side of the table, outside the viewer's own body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西被放到桌子对面，位于观看者身体之外。

branches.en: THE VIEW FROM OUTSIDE: impartial judgement and mind-independent reality both put the viewer on the far side of feeling.
branches.cn: 从外部观看：无偏判断与独立于心的现实，都把观看者置于情感之外。

branches.en: CHECKABLE EVIDENCE: data and physical proof are public objects that any observer can examine.
branches.cn: 可核查的证据：数据与物证是任何观察者都能查验的公共客体。

branches.en: THE TARGET AHEAD: a goal, and the function an algorithm moves toward, are objects set in front of the will.
branches.cn: 前方目标：目的以及算法所趋近的函数，都是摆在意志前方的客体。

branches.en: GRAMMATICAL OBJECT: the case that marks what the action is thrown against.
branches.cn: 语法宾语：标记动作所“对着”之物的格。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS AND SCORING: the lens facing the specimen and the test scored without a judge both remove the observer's private view.
branches.cn: 仪器与评分：正对标本的镜片、无需评判者的测试，都移除了观察者的私人视角。

intro.en: Objective is object plus -ive. The real engine of the family is ject-, the Latin 'throw' root, which combines with prefixes of direction to make a large set of English words.
intro.cn: objective 是 object 加 -ive。这个词族真正的发动机是 ject-，拉丁语“投掷”词根；它与表方向的前缀组合，构成一大批英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin obicere, objectum and the medieval objectivus are all attested; jacere is the base verb. Subicere supplies the mirror family with sub-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obicere、objectum 与中世纪 objectivus 均有文献可证；jacere 是基础动词。subicere 则以 sub- 提供镜像词族。

items.meaning: relating to an object; unbiased; goal (as a noun)
items.meaningCN: 与客体有关的；客观的；目标（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Keep the review objective and evidence-based.
items.exampleCN: 让评审保持客观并以证据为基础。

items.meaning: in an unbiased way
items.meaningCN: 客观地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: It is hard to judge your own work objectively.
items.exampleCN: 很难客观地评判自己的作品。

items.meaning: the quality of being objective
items.meaningCN: 客观性；客观态度（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The report was praised for its objectivity.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告因客观性受到称赞。

items.meaning: a thing perceived; to oppose
items.meaningCN: 物体；对象；反对（ob-“在前”+ ject“扔”）
items.example: Every object in the room was covered in dust.
items.exampleCN: 房间里的每件物品都落满了灰。

items.meaning: a reason for disagreeing
items.meaningCN: 反对；异议（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The lawyer raised an objection.
items.exampleCN: 律师提出了异议。

items.meaning: to treat a person as a thing
items.meaningCN: 使客体化；物化（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: The film was criticized for objectifying women.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影因物化女性受到批评。

items.meaning: the topic or the person under an authority
items.meaningCN: 主题；主体；臣民（sub-“在下”+ ject）
items.example: The subject of the lecture was memory.
items.exampleCN: 讲座的主题是记忆。

items.meaning: based on personal feeling
items.meaningCN: 主观的（sub- + ject + -ive）
items.example: Taste in music is subjective.
items.exampleCN: 音乐品味是主观的。

items.meaning: something thrown forward, such as an image or a forecast
items.meaningCN: 投影；预测（pro-“向前”+ ject + -ion）
items.example: The sales projection covers the next two years.
items.exampleCN: 销售预测覆盖未来两年。

items.meaning: to throw back; to refuse to accept
items.meaningCN: 拒绝；退回（re-“向后”+ ject“扔”）
items.example: The journal rejected the paper without review.
items.exampleCN: 期刊未经评审就退回了这篇论文。

latinEntries.meaning: to throw before; to present, oppose
that which is put before the mind
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被置于心智之前的事物

latinEntries.meaning: relating to an object of thought
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与思想对象有关的（中世纪拉丁语）

entry.definition_zh: 得到；取得；获得；（规则、习俗）通行、存在；可获得（obtainable）
entry.definition_en: to get or come into possession of something, especially through effort or request; of rules or customs, to be in force
entry.core_image: 把手伸过去，终于把东西握进自己掌中
entry.scene: After three visits to the office, he finally obtained the residence permit he needed to stay.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 obtain 是「取得、获得」（第 1 个义项：得到某物）；句意：跑了三趟办事处之后，他终于取得了继续居留所需的居住许可。图中可辨识物件：许可证、办事处窗口、排号单、护照。

pos.zh: 得到；取得；获得
（规则、习俗）通行；存在（正式用法）

derivatives.zh: 获得（罕用，多见于法律文本）
保持；维持；维护（同根 tain）

senses.title: Get or come into possession of something
senses.titleCN: 得到某物：进入占有状态
senses.definition: to get something that you did not have, usually by asking, applying, or working for it
senses.definitionCN: 得到原本没有的东西，通常通过申请、请求或努力
senses.example: You need to obtain a visa before you travel.
senses.exampleCN: 出行前你需要先取得签证。
senses.why: Latin obtinere is ob- 'toward' plus tenere 'to hold'. The old verb meant 'to hold fast, occupy'. Reaching toward a thing and holding it is the physical picture behind the modern 'get'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 是 ob-“朝向”加 tenere“握住”。古义为“握紧、占据”。朝某物伸手并把它握住，就是现代“得到”背后的动作画面。

senses.title: Obtain permission or approval
senses.definition: to succeed in getting official permission from a person or authority
senses.definitionCN: 成功从某人或某机构取得正式许可
senses.example: The researchers obtained permission to use the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员获得了使用该档案的许可。
senses.why: Permission is not a thing you can grab, but it is something granted into your keeping. Tenere 'hold' works because approval puts the right into your hands.
senses.whyCN: 许可不是能抓的实物，但它被授予后由你“持有”。tenere“握住”之所以适用，是因为批准把这项权利放进了你手里。

senses.title: Obtain results or data
senses.definition: to produce or arrive at a result, reading, or set of data through a procedure
senses.definitionCN: 通过某种程序产成或达到结果、读数或一组数据
senses.example: The same experiment obtained different results in two labs.
senses.exampleCN: 同一个实验在两个实验室得到了不同结果。
senses.why: In science the result is what the method yields. The word treats the outcome as something that comes into your hands from the procedure, so the 'hold' root is still felt.
senses.whyCN: 科学中结果是方法产出的东西。这个词把结果看作从程序来到你手中的东西，因此“握住”的词根仍可感知。

senses.title: Obtain a degree or qualification
senses.definition: to be awarded a degree, certificate, or professional qualification after completing requirements
senses.definitionCN: 完成要求后被授予学位、证书或职业资格
senses.example: She obtained a degree in economics before joining the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 进入银行工作前，她取得了经济学学位。
senses.why: A degree is held in the sense of possessing a status. The verb keeps the older 'possess' side of obtinere, which is why it suits titles and qualifications rather than only objects.
senses.whyCN: 学位是以“拥有一种身份”的方式被持有的。这个动词保留了 obtinere 较古老的“占有”一面，所以它适用于头衔与资格，而不只是实物。

senses.title: Obtain evidence: secure proof for a case
senses.titleCN: 取得证据：为案件获取证明
senses.definition: to get evidence, often formally, so that it can be used in an inquiry or trial
senses.definitionCN: 取得证据，常为正式途径，以便用于调查或审判
senses.example: Police obtained the evidence through a lawful search.
senses.exampleCN: 警方通过合法搜查取得了证据。
senses.why: Evidence must be 'held' before it can be presented. The legal register keeps the original sense of keeping something in hand, which is why obtain is common in formal and legal writing.
senses.whyCN: 证据必须先被“掌握”才能出示。法律语域保留了“把东西握在手里”的本义，所以 obtain 常见于正式与法律文本。

senses.title: Obtain by effort: earn through work
senses.definition: to gain something as a result of sustained effort rather than luck or a single request
senses.definitionCN: 因持续努力而非运气或一次请求而获得某物
senses.example: He obtained the position through years of night study.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过多年夜读获得了这个职位。
senses.why: The ob- prefix points toward a goal, and tenere supplies the grip. Together they describe reaching out and taking hold, an action that implies effort before possession.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 ob- 指向目标，tenere 提供“抓握”。两者合起来就是伸手并抓住，这个动作本身隐含了“占有之前要费力”。

senses.title: Obtain a patent or legal right
senses.definition: to be granted an exclusive legal right after an official application
senses.definitionCN: 经正式申请后被授予排他性的法律权利
senses.example: The company obtained a patent for the cooling device.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为这种冷却装置获得了专利。
senses.why: A patent is a right held against others, and obtinere in Latin could mean 'to hold, occupy'. The legal sense therefore continues the oldest meaning rather than the newer 'get'.
senses.whyCN: 专利是对他人主张的、由自己持有的权利，而拉丁语 obtinere 本可表示“持有、占据”。因此法律义延续的是最古老的含义，而非较新的“得到”。

senses.title: Of rules or customs: to be in force
senses.definition: of a rule, custom, or condition, to exist or remain established in a place
senses.definitionCN: 指规则、习俗或状况在某地存在或仍然确立
senses.example: The old custom still obtains in a few mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一古老习俗在少数山村仍然通行。
senses.why: This is the pure 'hold' sense: a custom that obtains holds its ground. English kept the Latin meaning 'be in force' alongside the newer 'acquire', which is why the verb can sound formal here.
senses.whyCN: 这是纯粹的“握住”义：一个 obtains 的习俗守住了它的地盘。英语在较新的“取得”之外保留了拉丁语“有效、成立”的含义，所以此处动词显得正式。

senses.title: Obtainable: available to be got
senses.definition: in the adjective obtainable, able to be got, bought, or reached
senses.definitionCN: 在形容词 obtainable 中，指能够被得到、买到或达到
senses.example: The drug is obtainable over the counter in some countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些国家，这种药无需处方即可买到。
senses.why: The suffix -able turns the verb into 'able to be obtained'. The same 'reach and hold' image now describes possibility rather than an act, which is a regular English suffix step.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把动词变成“能够被 obtain”。同一个“伸手并握住”的意象此刻描述的是可能性而非动作，这是英语常见的后缀派生步骤。

intro.en: Obtain is a Latin verb of holding that English borrowed through French. Its two modern branches, 'acquire' and 'be in force', are not a split in English; both were already present in the Latin verb.
intro.cn: obtain 是一个表示“握住”的拉丁动词，英语经法语借入。现代的两支——“取得”与“有效”——并非英语内部的分裂，两个含义在拉丁动词里就已存在。

items.en: The base verb tenere meant 'to hold, keep, grasp, occupy'. It is the source of the -tain in contain, maintain, retain, sustain and detain.
items.cn: 基础动词 tenere 意为“握住、保持、抓取、占据”。它是 contain、maintain、retain、sustain、detain 中 -tain 的来源。

items.en: The prefix ob- 'toward, against' was added to make obtinere, 'to hold fast, keep possession of, occupy'. The derivation step is prefix plus hold: reach toward and keep.
items.cn: 前缀 ob-“朝向、对着”加 tenere 构成 obtinere“握紧、保有、占据”。这一级派生是“前缀 + 握住”：朝之伸手并保持。

items.en: English records obtain in the early fifteenth century, borrowed through Middle French obtenir. The first English sense was 'to hold, possess, keep'.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪早期记录 obtain，经中古法语 obtenir 借入。最早的英语义是“持有、占有、保持”。

items.en: During the sixteenth century the main sense moved from 'hold what one has' to 'come to have what one did not'. The direction of ob- made this natural: reaching toward a thing ends in getting it.
items.cn: 16 世纪主要词义从“持有已有之物”转为“得到原本没有之物”。ob- 的方向使这一转变顺理成章：朝某物伸手，终点就是得到它。

items.en: Legal and official writing keeps the older 'hold, possess' shade: one obtains a judgment, an order, or a right. The same shade survives in the intransitive 'the rule obtains'.
items.cn: 法律与公文保留较古老的“持有、占有”色彩：obtain a judgment、an order、a right。同一色彩也保留在不及物的“the rule obtains”中。

items.en: The adjective obtainable is formed with -able in the nineteenth century; obtainment remains rare and mostly legal. Modern English uses obtain mostly in formal, academic, and legal registers.
items.cn: 形容词 obtainable 在 19 世纪由 -able 构成；obtainment 罕用且多限于法律文本。现代英语中 obtain 主要用于正式、学术和法律语域。

note.en: The look-alikes share -tain or a similar ending but differ in prefix and direction; the near meanings differ in how much effort or formality they imply.
note.cn: 形近词共享 -tain 或相似词尾，但前缀与方向不同；近义词的差别在于所含努力程度与正式程度。

entries.definition: to keep oneself away from something, such as alcohol or voting. It is abs- 'away from' + tenere 'hold'.
entries.definitionCN: 自我克制、不沾某物（如酒或投票）。它是 abs-“离开”+ tenere“握住”。

entries.definition: to hold something inside. It is con- 'together' + tenere, and is not a form of obtain.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物容纳在内。它是 con-“共同”+ tenere，并非 obtain 的变形。

entries.definition: to reach or achieve something after effort. It looks like obtain but comes from ad- + tangere 'to touch'.
entries.definitionCN: 经努力达到或实现。它形似 obtain，但来自 ad- + tangere“触碰”。

entries.definition: to gain something, often over time or by purchase. It stresses the process of coming to have.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物，常经时间或购买。它强调“逐渐拥有”的过程。

entries.definition: to get something valuable, especially an advantage or amount. It carries the idea of increase.
entries.definitionCN: 得到有价值之物，尤指优势或数量。它带有“增加”的意味。

entries.definition: to get something after overcoming difficulty or competition. It is stronger than obtain.
entries.definitionCN: 克服困难或竞争后得到某物。语气比 obtain 更强。

entries.definition: to obtain something, especially by deliberate action or for someone else. It is formal and often commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指通过刻意行动或为他人取得。它正式，常用于商业语境。

entries.definition: the everyday verb for coming to have something. It is the plain counterpart of the formal obtain.
entries.definitionCN: 得到某物的日常动词，是正式词 obtain 的平实对应。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the real tenere family and the two genuine Latin senses of obtinere; the sound hook is kept separate.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子使用真实的 tenere 词族和 obtinere 两个真实拉丁义项；谐音单独放置。

normal.en: tenere = hold. obtain = ob- 'toward' + hold: reach toward a thing until it is in your hand.
normal.cn: tenere = 握住。obtain = ob-“朝向”+ 握住：朝某物伸手，直到它落在你手里。

normal.en: The -tain family all keeps 'hold': contain holds inside, maintain holds up, retain holds back, detain holds away.
normal.cn: -tain 词族都保留“握”：contain 握在里面，maintain 握住不倒，retain 握住不放，detain 握住不让走。

normal.en: The rule obtains is not an odd exception: it is the oldest sense, where a custom 'holds its ground'.
normal.cn: the rule obtains 不是古怪的例外：它是最古老的义项——习俗“守住自己的地盘”。

normal.en: Because the word lives in formal writing, it pairs naturally with permission, evidence, a patent, a degree.
normal.cn: 因为这个词生活在正式文体里，它天然搭配 permission、evidence、a patent、a degree。

normal.en: obtainable is simply obtain + -able: able to be reached and held.
normal.cn: obtainable 就是 obtain + -able：能够被伸手够到并握住的。

abstract.en: Picture a hand crossing a table toward a document, fingers closing on it — the moment before is 'seeking', the moment after is 'obtaining'.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手越过桌面伸向一份文件、手指合拢——前一瞬是“寻求”，后一瞬就是“获得”。

abstract.en: The same grip explains the abstract cases: permission, a degree and a patent are all held rather than touched.
abstract.cn: 同一个“握”也解释了抽象用法：许可、学位、专利都是被“持有”的，而不是被摸到的。

abstract.en: The word never fully lost 'hold', which is why a custom can still obtain without anyone obtaining anything.
abstract.cn: 这个词从未彻底丢掉“握住”，所以习俗可以 obtain，却没有人 obtain 到任何东西。

examples.en: Further information can be obtained from the department office.
examples.cn: 更多信息可从系办公室获得。

examples.en: The team obtained funding for a second year of fieldwork.
examples.cn: 团队获得了第二年田野调查的经费。

examples.en: This practice no longer obtains in most cities.
examples.cn: 这一习俗在大多数城市已不再通行。

dict_mnemonic.text: “欧布TAIN”——“tain”听着像“拿”，欧布伸手一拿就 obtain（得到）

entry.root: 拉丁 ob-“朝向”+ tenere“握住”→ obtinere“握紧、保有、占据”；英语经法语借入后主要义转为“取得”，而“有效、通行”保留了古老的“守住”义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one hand: it reaches toward something (ob-) and closes on it (tenere). What is reached may be a visa, a permission, a result, a degree, proof, a post, a patent, a custom, or simply a possibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟随同一只手：朝某物伸去（ob-），然后合拢握住（tenere）。被够到的可以是签证、许可、结果、学位、证据、职位、专利、习俗，甚至只是一种可能性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches across and closes on what it wanted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸过去，合拢抓住想要的东西。

branches.en: THE BASIC GRIP: the general sense of coming into possession, from which the formal uses branch.
branches.cn: 基本抓握：进入占有状态的总义，正式用法都由此分出。

branches.en: RIGHTS AND PROOF: permission, evidence and a patent are held rather than touched, so legal writing keeps the old 'possess' shade.
branches.cn: 权利与证明：许可、证据、专利是被持有而非被触摸的，所以法律文体保留古老的“占有”色彩。

branches.en: WHAT A PROCESS YIELDS: results and degrees arrive from a procedure or a course of study into the holder's hands.
branches.cn: 过程所产出之物：结果与学位从程序或学业来到持有者手中。

branches.en: EFFORT BEFORE POSSESSION: ob- points at the goal, and the grip is earned rather than given.
branches.cn: 占有之前的努力：ob- 指向目标，而这一握是靠努力挣来的，不是被给予的。

branches.en: HOLDING GROUND AND POSSIBILITY: a custom still 'holds', and -able turns the grip into 'can be got'.
branches.cn: 守住地盘与可能性：习俗仍然“守住”，而 -able 把这一握变成“能被得到”。

intro.en: Obtain is a prefix plus a Latin verb stem. The stem -tain is not a free English word, but it is the shared engine of a whole family of hold- verbs.
intro.cn: obtain 是前缀加拉丁动词词干。词干 -tain 不是独立的英语单词，却是整个“握”系动词家族共同的发动机。

latinIntro.en: Latin obtinere and tenere are both attested, as are abstinere, continere and detinere. The prefixes in the English family still show direction: together, up, back, away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obtinere 与 tenere 均有文献可证，abstinere、continere、detinere 亦然。英语词族中的前缀仍显示方向：共同、向上、向后、离开。

items.meaning: to come into possession of; to be in force
items.meaningCN: 取得；占有；（规则）有效（ob- + tain“握”）
items.example: She obtained a copy of the report.
items.exampleCN: 她取得了一份报告副本。

items.meaning: able to be got or bought
items.meaningCN: 可获得的；买得到的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: Tickets are obtainable at the door.
items.exampleCN: 门票可在门口买到。

items.meaning: the act of obtaining, rare outside legal texts
items.meaningCN: 获得（罕用，多见于法律文本；-ment 构成行为名词）
items.example: The obtainment of a licence requires two inspections.
items.exampleCN: 取得执照需要两次检查。

items.meaning: to hold inside; to keep within limits
items.meaningCN: 包含；容纳；控制（con-“共同”+ tain“握”）
items.example: The box contains old letters.
items.exampleCN: 箱子里装着旧信件。

items.meaning: to keep in good condition; to keep a claim
items.meaningCN: 维持；保养；坚持主张（main“手”+ tain“握”）
items.example: They maintain the road every spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天维护这条路。

items.meaning: to keep or hold on to something
items.meaningCN: 保留；留住（re-“向后”+ tain“握”）
items.example: The soil retains water well.
items.exampleCN: 这种土壤保水性好。

items.meaning: to hold up; to keep going over time
items.meaningCN: 支撑；维持（sus-“从下方托起”+ tain“握”）
items.example: The bridge cannot sustain that weight.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥承受不了那样的重量。

items.meaning: to keep someone from leaving
items.meaningCN: 扣留；耽搁（de-“离开”+ tain“握”）
items.example: Police detained two men for questioning.
items.exampleCN: 警方扣留了两名男子问话。

items.meaning: to hold oneself back from something
items.meaningCN: 克制；弃权（abs-“离开”+ tain“握”）
items.example: Three members abstained from the vote.
items.exampleCN: 三名成员投了弃权票。

items.meaning: a person who holds a rented property
items.meaningCN: 承租人；租户（ten-“持有”+ -ant 表人）
items.example: The tenant pays rent on the first of the month.
items.exampleCN: 租户每月一号交房租。

latinEntries.meaning: to hold fast, possess; to prevail

entry.definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；容易理解的；不证自明的
entry.definition_en: easy to see, notice, or understand, because nothing hides it and no effort is needed to find it
entry.core_image: 一件东西正好挡在你走的路上：你还没找，它就撞进了眼里
entry.scene: The cracked step was obvious to everyone at the entrance, yet nobody had reported it for weeks.
entry.sceneCN: 这里 obvious 是「显而易见的」（第 1 个义项：很容易看见、注意到）；句意：入口处那级裂开的台阶人人都看得见，却有几周没人上报。图中可辨识物件：裂开的台阶、入口门、行人、警示牌。

pos.zh: 明显的；显而易见的；容易理解的
不证自明的；不言而喻的

senses.title: Easy to see or notice: right in front of you
senses.definition: so plainly visible or noticeable that it needs no searching
senses.definitionCN: 明显可见或显眼，无需寻找就能注意到
senses.example: There was an obvious crack in the windscreen.
senses.exampleCN: 挡风玻璃上有一道明显的裂缝。
senses.why: Latin obvius means 'in the way, meeting one on the road', from ob- 'in front of' plus via 'road'. What lies in your path is seen before you look for it, so 'in the way' becomes 'easily seen'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 意为“挡在路上、在途中迎面遇到”，由 ob-“在前”加 via“路”构成。挡在你路上的东西，在你找之前就已被看见，于是“挡路”变成“易见”。

senses.title: Easy to understand: no explanation needed
senses.definition: so clear to the mind that it can be grasped at once
senses.definitionCN: 对心智而言清楚到可以立刻把握
senses.example: The answer was obvious once the diagram was drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 画出图之后，答案就显而易见了。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from the road to reasoning: an idea that stands in the path of thought is met without a detour. Seeing and understanding use the same image of 'nothing in the way'.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从道路移到了推理：挡在思路上的想法，不用绕路就会遇到。看见与理解共用同一个“前方无阻”的意象。

senses.title: The obvious choice: the one that presents itself
senses.titleCN: 显而易见的选择：自己送上门的那个
senses.definition: the option that seems clearly right without comparing many alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 无需比较许多备选就显得明确正确的选项
senses.example: The obvious choice was to take the earlier train.
senses.exampleCN: 显而易见的选择是坐早一班火车。
senses.why: An option that 'meets you on the road' needs no search. The word marks the candidate that presents itself first, not necessarily the best one.
senses.whyCN: 一个“在路上迎着你来”的选项不需要寻找。这个词标记的是最先自己呈现的候选，而不必然是最好的那个。

senses.title: The obvious question: the one anyone would ask
senses.titleCN: 显而易见的问题：谁都会问的那个
senses.definition: the question that naturally arises and hardly needs to be pointed out
senses.definitionCN: 自然浮现、几乎无需指明的问题
senses.example: The obvious question is who will pay for the repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 显而易见的问题是：谁来付修理费。
senses.why: Here the word applies to something expected rather than seen. If the question is already in everyone's path, asking it aloud adds nothing new.
senses.whyCN: 此处这个词用于“预期之物”而非“所见之物”。如果问题已在所有人的路上，大声问出来并不增加新东西。

senses.title: An obvious fact: plainly true
senses.definition: a fact so clear and widely accepted that it can be stated without proof
senses.definitionCN: 清楚且被广泛接受、无需证明即可陈述的事实
senses.example: It is an obvious fact that water boils at a lower temperature at altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 水在海拔高处沸点更低，这是一个明显的事实。
senses.why: A fact is 'obvious' when it stands in the open, exposed to anyone's view. The root's physical openness is transferred to truth: nothing conceals it.
senses.whyCN: 事实之所以“明显”，是因为它摆在明处，任何人都看得见。词根中“暴露于外”的物理义被转用到真相上：没有任何东西遮住它。

senses.title: Obvious to everyone: public and undeniable
senses.titleCN: 人人都看得出：公开且不可否认
senses.definition: used with 'to' to say that a whole group can perceive or recognise something
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，表示一群人都能察觉或承认某事
senses.example: It was obvious to everyone that she had not slept.
senses.exampleCN: 人人都看得出她没睡过觉。
senses.why: Obvius described something that meets people on a public road, not a private one. Because the road is shared, what is obvious is visible to all, and the word suggests agreement rather than mere visibility.
senses.whyCN: obvius 描述的是在公共道路上迎人而来的东西，而不是私人的路。路是共享的，所以 obvious 之物众人可见，这个词也暗示着共识，而不只是“看得见”。

senses.title: The obvious answer: the direct solution
senses.titleCN: 明显的答案：直接的解法
senses.definition: the solution that is simplest and most direct, sometimes overlooked because it is too simple
senses.definitionCN: 最简单直接的解法，有时因过于简单反被忽略
senses.example: The obvious answer is to turn it off and turn it on again.
senses.exampleCN: 明显的答案是关掉再开一次。
senses.why: Anything lying in the road is reached first; the direct solution is therefore 'obvious' even when people prefer a complicated detour.
senses.whyCN: 躺在路上的东西总是最先被走到；直接解法因此是“明显”的，哪怕人们偏爱复杂的绕路。

senses.title: An obvious risk: plainly foreseeable
senses.titleCN: 明显的风险：明摆着的隐患
senses.definition: a danger that is easy to foresee and therefore hard to excuse ignoring
senses.definitionCN: 容易预见、因而难以辩解忽视的危险
senses.example: There was an obvious risk in lending him the money.
senses.exampleCN: 把钱借给他有明显的风险。
senses.why: A risk in your path is one you cannot claim not to have seen. 'Obvious' here works as a judgement on the observer: the danger was open, so ignoring it was a choice.
senses.whyCN: 风险挡在路上，你就不能声称自己没看见。obvious 在此是对观察者的评判：危险既在明处，忽视它便是一种选择。

senses.title: State the obvious: say what needs no saying
senses.titleCN: 明说显而易见之事：说无需说的话
senses.definition: in the phrase state the obvious, to point out something that everyone already knows
senses.definitionCN: 用于 state the obvious，指出人人都已知道的事
senses.example: He was only stating the obvious: the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是在说显而易见的事：计划失败了。
senses.why: The phrase turns the adjective into a noun, 'the obvious', meaning everything that lies in plain view. To state it is to read aloud what the road already shows.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把形容词名词化为 the obvious，指一切摆在明处的东西。state 它，就是把路已经显示的东西念出来。

intro.en: Obvious is a road word before it is a thinking word. Latin via 'road' plus ob- 'in front of' produces obvius, 'in the way'; English adds -ous, and the sense shifts from physical obstruction to plain visibility.
intro.cn: obvious 先是道路词，后才是思维词。拉丁语 via“路”加 ob-“在前”构成 obvius“挡在路上”；英语加 -ous 作形容词，词义再从物理阻挡转为“清楚可见”。

items.en: via meant 'way, road, street, path'. It is the base noun of a whole road family: deviate, previous, trivial, impervious.
items.cn: via 意为“道路、路、街、路径”。它是整个“路”词族的基础名词：deviate、previous、trivial、impervious。

items.en: ob- 'in front of, against, on the way of' plus via gives obvius, 'placed in the way, meeting one on the road'. The derivation is positional: a thing standing where you must pass.
items.cn: ob-“在前、对着、挡在……路上”加 via 构成 obvius“挡在路上、在途中迎面遇到的”。这一级派生是位置性的：东西立在你必须经过的地方。

items.en: Latin also had obviam ire 'to go to meet', and the verb obviare 'to meet, oppose, prevent'. This is the source of English obviate, a separate word from the same road image.
items.cn: 拉丁语还有 obviam ire“前去迎接”，以及动词 obviare“迎上、对抗、阻止”。这是英语 obviate 的来源，它与 obvious 同出一个道路意象，却是另一个词。

items.en: English records obvious in the 1580s, meaning 'in the way, presenting itself, easily seen'. The -ous ending is the ordinary English adjective suffix added to the Latin stem.
items.cn: 英语在 1580 年代记录 obvious，义为“挡在路上、自行呈现、容易看见”。-ous 是加在拉丁词干上的普通英语形容词后缀。

items.en: The older literal sense 'standing in the way, opposing' dies out, and the word settles on what is open to view and therefore plain. The obstruction disappears; only the visibility remains.
items.cn: 较古老的实义“阻挡、对抗”消失，词义固定为“暴露于视野、因而清楚”。阻挡义隐去，只留下可见性。

items.en: Modern English builds obviously and obviousness by ordinary suffixes, and fixes the phrase state the obvious. Obviate survives as a formal verb meaning 'to prevent or remove'.
items.cn: 现代英语用普通后缀构成 obviously 与 obviousness，并固定短语 state the obvious。obviate 作为正式动词保留下来，意为“防止、消除”。

note.en: The look-alikes below are spelling neighbours, not meaning neighbours; note that oblivious is almost the opposite of obvious in actual use.
note.cn: 下面的形近词只是拼写邻居，不是意义邻居；注意 oblivious 在实际使用中几乎与 obvious 相反。

entries.definition: not aware of what is happening. It comes from oblivio 'forgetfulness', not from via, and means nearly the reverse of obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 对正在发生的事毫无察觉。它来自 oblivio“遗忘”，而非 via，含义几乎与 obvious 相反。

entries.definition: to prevent or remove a difficulty in advance. It is the verb from obviam ire, 'to go to meet'.
entries.definitionCN: 提前防止或消除困难。它是来自 obviam ire“前去迎接”的动词。

entries.definition: coming before in time. It is prae- 'before' + via 'road', literally 'going before on the road'.
entries.definitionCN: 时间上在先的。它是 prae-“在前”+ via“路”，字面为“在路上走在前头”。

entries.definition: clear from the available evidence. It is slightly more formal and more argument-based than obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 从现有证据看很清楚。它比 obvious 略正式，也更依赖论证。

entries.definition: easily seen, but sometimes only seemingly true. It carries a hint of 'as it appears, not as it is'.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见的，但有时只是表面上为真。它带有“看似如此、未必如此”的暗示。

entries.definition: easy to see, hear, or understand. It is the broad word; obvious adds that no search was needed.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见或理解的。它是最宽泛的词；obvious 额外强调“无需寻找”。

entries.definition: simple and undecorated, hence easy to understand. It stresses absence of complication rather than presence in view.
entries.definitionCN: 简单无装饰，因而易懂。它强调“没有复杂之处”，而非“就在视野中”。

entries.definition: clearly shown or displayed. It is formal and often used of qualities or symptoms.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚显示出来的。它正式，常用于品质或症状。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the real via family and the literal road image; the sound hook is labelled separately.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子依据真实的 via 词族与字面上的道路意象；谐音钩子单独标注。

normal.en: ob- 'in front' + via 'road' = 'in the road'. Something in your road is seen before you look for it.
normal.cn: ob-“在前”+ via“路”=“在路上”。挡在你路上的东西，在你寻找之前就被看见。

normal.en: One via family, many directions: deviate turns off the road, previous goes before, trivial is the three-way crossroads, impervious has no way through.
normal.cn: 一个 via 词族，许多方向：deviate 离开道路，previous 走在前头，trivial 是三条路交叉口，impervious 无路可通。

normal.en: Obviate is the sibling verb: to go and meet a problem on the road is to prevent it.
normal.cn: obviate 是兄弟动词：在路上去迎上一个问题，就是提前阻止它。

normal.en: Oblivious looks like obvious but is its opposite: not 'in the road before you' but 'washed out of memory'.
normal.cn: oblivious 形似 obvious 却是反义：不是“摆在路前”，而是“被遗忘冲走”。

normal.en: The 17c change dropped the idea of blocking and kept only the idea of being seen, which is why obvious no longer means 'in the way'.
normal.cn: 17 世纪的转变丢掉了“阻挡”，只留下“被看见”，所以 obvious 不再表示“挡路”。

abstract.en: Picture walking down a lane at night with a lamp: whatever the lamp hits first is obvious, and you never had to search for it.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里提灯走在小路上：灯最先照到的东西就是 obvious，你从未需要去寻找它。

abstract.en: Move the same lamp from a road to an argument, and 'first thing met' becomes 'first thing understood'.
abstract.cn: 把同一盏灯从道路移到论证上，“最先遇到之物”就变成“最先理解之物”。

abstract.en: The word's sting is social: what is obvious to all makes ignoring it a choice, which is why obvious risks are hard to excuse.
abstract.cn: 这个词的锋芒在社会层面：人人都 obvious 的事，使“忽视”成为一种选择，所以明显的风险难以辩解。

examples.en: For obvious reasons, the meeting was moved online.
examples.cn: 由于显而易见的原因，会议改到线上。

examples.en: It soon became obvious that the two accounts did not match.
examples.cn: 很快就明显了：两份账目对不上。

examples.en: The solution looks obvious only after someone else has found it.
examples.cn: 答案只有在别人找到之后才显得显而易见。

dict_mnemonic.text: “偶不V啊死”——“这不 obvious 吗！”一眼就看见，明显得很

entry.root: 拉丁 ob-“在前、挡在路上”+ via“路”→ obvius“挡在路上、迎面遇到的”→ 英语加 -ous →“摆在眼前的、显而易见的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one scene: something stands in the road you are walking. Because it is already in your path, it is seen, understood, chosen, asked, feared or stated without any search.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共守一个场景：有东西立在你正走的路上。因为它已在你的路径中，所以无需寻找就被看见、被理解、被选择、被提问、被担忧或被说出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object standing in the middle of the road, hit by your light before you search.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西立在路中央，在你寻找之前就被你的灯照到。

branches.en: OPEN TO THE EYE: a crack or a fact lies in plain view, so no one has to point at it.
branches.cn: 暴露于眼：裂缝或事实摆在明处，无需有人指出。

branches.en: OPEN TO THE MIND: understanding and the direct solution are met without a detour.
branches.cn: 暴露于心：理解与直接解法不用绕路就能遇到。

branches.en: WHAT PRESENTS ITSELF FIRST: the obvious choice and the obvious question are the candidates that step forward on their own.
branches.cn: 最先自行呈现之物：显而易见的选择与问题，是自己走上前来的候选。

branches.en: SHARED ROAD: because the road is public, what is obvious is visible to all and invites agreement.
branches.cn: 共享之路：路是公共的，所以 obvious 之物众人可见，也带来共识。

branches.en: NO EXCUSE AND NO NEWS: a risk in the road cannot be pleaded unseen, and stating the obvious says nothing new.
branches.cn: 无从辩解、也无新意：路上的风险不能声称没看见，而 state the obvious 等于没说新东西。

intro.en: Obvious is a Latin stem plus the English adjective suffix -ous. The stem itself is a preposition plus a noun, so the word's whole meaning is a spatial relation.
intro.cn: obvious 是拉丁词干加英语形容词后缀 -ous。词干本身是“介词 + 名词”，所以整个词义就是一个空间关系。

latinIntro.en: Latin via, obvius and obviare are attested; devius 'off the road' supplies the negative branch. English keeps the road image alive in a large family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 via、obvius、obviare 均有文献可证；devius“离开道路的”提供否定分支。英语让这个道路意象在大家族中继续存活。

items.meaning: in the way; plain to see
items.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；显而易见的（ob- + via + -ous）
items.example: The error was obvious to the reader.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误读者一眼就能看出。

items.meaning: plainly; as anyone can see
items.meaningCN: 显然；明显地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She was obviously tired.
items.exampleCN: 她显然累了。

items.meaning: the quality of being plain to see
items.meaningCN: 显而易见；明显性（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: The obviousness of the answer made them suspicious.
items.exampleCN: 答案过于显而易见，反而让他们起疑。

items.meaning: to meet and remove a difficulty in advance
items.meaningCN: 消除；排除（提前迎上困难；ob- + via + -ate）
items.example: A backup generator obviates the need for candles.
items.exampleCN: 备用发电机免去了点蜡烛的必要。

items.structure: Latin noun used in English as a preposition
items.meaning: by way of; through
items.meaningCN: 经由；通过（拉丁名词 via“路”直接用作介词）
items.example: We flew to Rome via Paris.
items.exampleCN: 我们经巴黎飞往罗马。

items.meaning: going before on the road; earlier
items.meaningCN: 走在前面的；先前的（prae- + via + -ous）
items.example: The previous owner kept the keys.
items.exampleCN: 前房主留着那些钥匙。

items.meaning: to turn off the road; to depart from a standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；背离（de-“离开”+ via + -ate）
items.example: The plane deviated from its course.
items.exampleCN: 飞机偏离了航线。

items.meaning: of the three-way crossroads; hence commonplace, unimportant
items.meaningCN: 三岔路口的；因而平常、琐碎的（tri- + via + -al）
items.example: They argued over trivial details.
items.exampleCN: 他们为琐碎细节争吵。

items.meaning: having no way through; unaffected
items.meaningCN: 无法穿透的；不受影响的（im- + per- + via + -ous）
items.example: The coat is impervious to rain.
items.exampleCN: 这件外套防雨。

items.meaning: off the straight road; indirect or dishonest
items.meaningCN: 离开直路的；迂回的、不诚实的（de- + via + -ous）
items.example: They took a devious route through the back streets.
items.exampleCN: 他们走后街绕了一条迂回的路。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；迎面遇到的
